src/mesh.c:29:      for (int x = 0; x < 16; x++) {

src/mesh.c:67:
src/mesh.c:68:// Restricts a column mask (bits 0..17) to just the 16 bits that map to
src/mesh.c:69:// this block's own local nodes (bits 1..16) -- bits 0 and 17 are the
src/mesh.c:70:// neighbor's border, only used below to determine whether a boundary face
src/mesh.c:71:// exists, never as a face position themselves.
src/mesh.c:72:#define INTERIOR_MASK 0x1FFFEu
src/mesh.c:73:
src/mesh.c:74:// Maps (axis, a, b, n) back to the full local (x, y, z) it represents,
src/mesh.c:75:// using occupancy_build's own cols[axis][a][b] convention. Shared by both
src/mesh.c:76:// the face-grid extraction and the quad emission below so the two can't
src/mesh.c:77:// drift apart from each other.
src/mesh.c:78:static void axis_to_xyz(int axis, int a, int b, int n, int *x, int *y,
src/mesh.c:79:                         int *z) {
src/mesh.c:80:  switch (axis) {
src/mesh.c:81:  case 0:
src/mesh.c:82:    *x = n;
src/mesh.c:83:    *y = a;
src/mesh.c:84:    *z = b;
src/mesh.c:85:    break;
src/mesh.c:86:  case 1:
src/mesh.c:87:    *x = a;
src/mesh.c:88:    *y = n;
src/mesh.c:89:    *z = b;
src/mesh.c:90:    break;
src/mesh.c:91:  default: // 2
src/mesh.c:92:    *x = a;
src/mesh.c:93:    *y = b;
src/mesh.c:94:    *z = n;
src/mesh.c:95:    break;
src/mesh.c:96:  }
src/mesh.c:97:}
src/mesh.c:98:
src/mesh.c:99:// Extracts a 16x16 (present, content_id) grid for one axis/direction/depth
src/mesh.c:100:// combination: present[a][b] is true if a face exists at local depth `n`
src/mesh.c:101:// on `direction`'s side, and content[a][b] is the content id of the solid
src/mesh.c:102:// node the face belongs to (undefined where present[a][b] is false).
src/mesh.c:103:static void build_face_grid(uint32_t occ_col[16][16], int axis,
src/mesh.c:104:                             int direction, int n, const Mapblock *own,
src/mesh.c:105:                             bool present[16][16], uint16_t content[16][16]) {
src/mesh.c:106:  for (int a = 0; a < 16; a++) {
src/mesh.c:107:    for (int b = 0; b < 16; b++) {
src/mesh.c:108:      uint32_t col = occ_col[a][b];
src/mesh.c:109:      // direction 0 (negative-facing): solid at i, non-solid at i-1.
src/mesh.c:110:      // direction 1 (positive-facing): solid at i, non-solid at i+1.
src/mesh.c:111:      uint32_t faces = direction == 0 ? (col & ~(col << 1)) & INTERIOR_MASK
src/mesh.c:112:                                       : (col & ~(col >> 1)) & INTERIOR_MASK;
src/mesh.c:113:      bool has_face = (faces & (1u << (n + 1))) != 0;
src/mesh.c:114:      present[a][b] = has_face;
src/mesh.c:115:      if (has_face) {
src/mesh.c:116:        int x, y, z;
src/mesh.c:117:        axis_to_xyz(axis, a, b, n, &x, &y, &z);
src/mesh.c:118:        content[a][b] = mapblock_get(own, x, y, z).content_id;
src/mesh.c:119:      }
src/mesh.c:120:    }
src/mesh.c:121:  }
src/mesh.c:122:}
src/mesh.c:123:
src/mesh.c:124:// 2D greedy rectangle merge over one axis/direction/depth plane. For each
src/mesh.c:125:// unvisited present cell: grow a run along `a` while content keeps
src/mesh.c:126:// matching, then grow along `b` while every cell in the current a-range
src/mesh.c:127:// still matches at that b -- the standard "grow one axis, then grow the
src/mesh.c:128:// other only while the whole strip agrees" greedy-meshing merge, not the
src/mesh.c:129:// (harder, unnecessary at 16x16) fully general maximal-rectangle solve.
src/mesh.c:130:static void merge_plane(bool present[16][16], uint16_t content[16][16],
src/mesh.c:131:                         int axis, int direction, int n, Mesh *out) {
src/mesh.c:132:  bool visited[16][16] = {0};
src/mesh.c:133:  for (int a = 0; a < 16; a++) {
src/mesh.c:134:    for (int b = 0; b < 16; b++) {
src/mesh.c:135:      if (visited[a][b] || !present[a][b]) {
src/mesh.c:136:        continue;
src/mesh.c:137:      }
src/mesh.c:138:      uint16_t id = content[a][b];
src/mesh.c:139:
src/mesh.c:140:      int height = 1; // extent along `a`
src/mesh.c:141:      while (a + height < 16 && !visited[a + height][b] &&
src/mesh.c:142:             present[a + height][b] && content[a + height][b] == id) {
src/mesh.c:143:        height++;
src/mesh.c:144:      }
src/mesh.c:145:
src/mesh.c:146:      int width = 1; // extent along `b`
src/mesh.c:147:      while (b + width < 16) {
src/mesh.c:148:        bool strip_matches = true;
src/mesh.c:149:        for (int da = 0; da < height; da++) {
src/mesh.c:150:          if (visited[a + da][b + width] || !present[a + da][b + width] ||
src/mesh.c:151:              content[a + da][b + width] != id) {
src/mesh.c:152:            strip_matches = false;
src/mesh.c:153:            break;
src/mesh.c:154:          }
src/mesh.c:155:        }
src/mesh.c:156:        if (!strip_matches) {
src/mesh.c:157:          break;
src/mesh.c:158:        }
src/mesh.c:159:        width++;
src/mesh.c:160:      }
src/mesh.c:161:
src/mesh.c:162:      for (int da = 0; da < height; da++) {
src/mesh.c:163:        for (int db = 0; db < width; db++) {
src/mesh.c:164:          visited[a + da][b + db] = true;
src/mesh.c:165:        }
src/mesh.c:166:      }
src/mesh.c:167:
src/mesh.c:168:      if (out->count >= out->capacity) {
src/mesh.c:169:        fprintf(stderr, "merge_plane: quad output exceeded capacity %u\n",
src/mesh.c:170:                out->capacity);
src/mesh.c:171:        exit(1);
src/mesh.c:172:      }
src/mesh.c:173:      int x, y, z;
src/mesh.c:174:      axis_to_xyz(axis, a, b, n, &x, &y, &z);
src/mesh.c:175:      out->quads[out->count++] = (Quad){
src/mesh.c:176:          .x = (uint8_t)x,
src/mesh.c:177:          .y = (uint8_t)y,
src/mesh.c:178:          .z = (uint8_t)z,
src/mesh.c:179:          .width = (uint8_t)width,
src/mesh.c:180:          .height = (uint8_t)height,
src/mesh.c:181:          .axis = (uint8_t)axis,
src/mesh.c:182:          .direction = (uint8_t)direction,
src/mesh.c:183:          .content_id = id,
src/mesh.c:184:      };
src/mesh.c:185:    }
src/mesh.c:186:  }
src/mesh.c:187:}

src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:882:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:883:  /* Reflecting off a "horizontal" surface in 2D */

src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:885:  vec2 N1 = {0.0f, 1.0f};  /* Normal vector */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:886:  GLM(vec2_reflect)(I1, N1, dest);

src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:888:         fabsf(dest[1] - 1.0f) < 0.00001f); /* Expect reflection upwards */

src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:892:  vec2 N2 = {0.0f, 1.0f}; /* Upwards normal vector */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:893:  GLM(vec2_reflect)(I2, N2, dest);

src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:896:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:897:  /* Reflecting off a line in 2D representing a "vertical" surface analogy */

src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec2.h:917:  // In 2D, we expect a similar bending behavior as in 3D, so we check dest[1]

src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1985:TEST_IMPL(GLM_PREFIX, vec3_refract) {
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1986:  vec3  v = {sqrtf(0.5f), -sqrtf(0.5f), 0.0f}; /* Incoming vector at 45 degrees to normal */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1987:  vec3  N = {0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f};                /* Surface normal */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1988:  vec3  dest;
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1989:  float eta;
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1990:  bool  r;
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1991:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1992:  /* Water to Air (eta = 1.33/1.0) */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1993:  eta = 1.33f / 1.0f;
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1994:  r = GLM(vec3_refract)(v, N, eta, dest);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1995:  if (!(dest[0] == 0.0f && dest[1] == 0.0f && dest[2] == 0.0f)) {
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1996:    ASSERT(dest[1] < -0.3f);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1997:    ASSERT(r == true);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1998:  } else {
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:1999:    ASSERT(dest[0] == 0.0f && dest[1] == 0.0f && dest[2] == 0.0f);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2000:    ASSERT(r == false);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2001:  }
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2002:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2003:  /* Air to Glass (eta = 1.0 / 1.5) */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2004:  eta = 1.0f / 1.5f;
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2005:  r = GLM(vec3_refract)(v, N, eta, dest);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2006:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2007:  /* Expect bending towards the normal */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2008:  ASSERT(r == true);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2009:  ASSERT(dest[1] < -sqrtf(0.5f));
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2010:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2011:  /* Glass to Water (eta = 1.5 / 1.33) */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2012:  eta = 1.5f / 1.33f;
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2013:  r = GLM(vec3_refract)(v, N, eta, dest);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2014:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2015:  /* Expect bending towards the normal, less bending than air to glass */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2016:  ASSERT(r == true);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2017:  ASSERT(dest[1] < -0.6f);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2018:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2019:  /* Diamond to Air (eta = 2.42 / 1.0) */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2020:  eta = 2.42f / 1.0f;
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2021:  r = GLM(vec3_refract)(v, N, eta, dest);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2022:  if (!(dest[0] == 0.0f && dest[1] == 0.0f && dest[2] == 0.0f)) {
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2023:    /* High potential for total internal reflection, but if it occurs, expect significant bending */
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2024:    ASSERT(dest[1] < -sqrtf(0.5f));
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2025:    ASSERT(r == true);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2026:  } else {
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2027:    ASSERT(dest[0] == 0.0f && dest[1] == 0.0f && dest[2] == 0.0f);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2028:    ASSERT(r == false);
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2029:  }
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2030:
src/third_party/cglm/test/src/test_vec3.h:2031:  TEST_SUCCESS

src/third_party/cglm/BUILDING.md:62:Since math functions like `sinf` are used, this can not be targeted at `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, one of [wasi-sdk](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasi-sdk) or [emscripten](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk) should be used.
src/third_party/cglm/BUILDING.md:63:
src/third_party/cglm/BUILDING.md:64:Should note that shared build is not yet supported for WebAssembly.
src/third_party/cglm/BUILDING.md:65:
src/third_party/cglm/BUILDING.md:66:For [simd128](https://github.com/WebAssembly/simd) support, add `-msimd128` to `CMAKE_C_FLAGS`, in command line `-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-msimd128"`.
src/third_party/cglm/BUILDING.md:67:
src/third_party/cglm/BUILDING.md:68:For tests, the cmake option `CGLM_USE_TEST` would still work, you'll need a wasi runtime for running tests, see our [ci config file](.github/workflows/cmake-wasm.yml) for a detailed example.

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:42:A highly optimized 2D|3D math library. Also known as OpenGL Mathematics (glm) for C. <b>cglm</b> provides fast and ergonomic math functions to ease graphics programming. It is community friendly – feel free to report any bugs and issues you face. <br>
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:43:<i>If you're using C++, you might want to check out <a href="https://github.com/g-truc/glm">GLM</a></i>
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:44:</p>

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:47: - Header-only
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:48: - SIMD-optimized
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:49: - API-agnostic

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:59:

If you wish to link against it instead, it can be built using one of the supported build systems. Detailed information about building on individual platforms and build systems along with the instructions for building the documentation can be found in [BUILDING.md](./BUILDING.md).

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:64:#### Header-only
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:65:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:66:Include the `cglm/cglm.h` header and use functions with the `glm_` prefix.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:67:```c
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:68:#include "cglm/cglm.h"
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:69:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:70:// ...
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:71:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:72:vec2 vector;
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:73:glm_vec2_zero(vector);
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:74:```
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:75:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:76:#### Struct API
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:77:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:78:Include `cglm/struct.h` and use `glms_`.

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:80:#include "cglm/struct.h"
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:81:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:82:// ...
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:83:

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:99:### ❗ Alignment
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:100:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:101:While cglm by default aligns what's necessary, it is possible to disable this by defining `CGLM_ALL_UNALIGNED`. If you're targeting machines with any kind of SIMD support, make sure that all `vec4`, `mat4` and `mat2` arguments you pass to cglm functions are aligned to prevent unexpected crashes, alternatively use the unaligned versions if present. 
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:102:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:103:### Struct API
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:104:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:105:The struct API works as follows (note the `s` suffix on types, `glms_` prefix on functions and `GLMS_` on constants):
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:106:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:107:```C
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:108:#include <cglm/struct.h>
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:109:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:110:mat4s mat = GLMS_MAT4_IDENTITY_INIT;
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:111:mat4s inv = glms_mat4_inv(mat);
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:112:```
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:113:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:114:Struct functions generally take parameters *by copy* and *return* the results rather than taking pointers and writing to out parameters. That means your variables can usually be `const`, if you're into that.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:115:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:116:The types used are actually unions that allow access to the same data in multiple ways. One of these involves anonymous structures available since C11. MSVC supports them in earlier versions out of the box and GCC/Clang as well if you enable `-fms-extensions`.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:117:To explicitly enable anonymous structures `#define CGLM_USE_ANONYMOUS_STRUCT 1`, or `0` to disable them.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:118:For backwards compatibility, you can also `#define CGLM_NO_ANONYMOUS_STRUCT` to disable them. If you don't specify explicitly, cglm will attempt a best guess based on your compiler and C version.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:119:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:120:### 📌 Migration notes:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:121:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:122:- `_dup` (duplicate) functions were renamed to `_copy`. For instance: `glm_vec_dup` -> `glm_vec3_copy`.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:123:- OpenGL related functions were dropped to make cglm API independent.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:124:- **[bugfix]** Euler angles had been previously implemented in reverse order (extrinsic). This was fixed to be intrinsic.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:125:- **[major change]** Starting with **v0.4.0**, quaternions are stored as [x, y, z, w]. Previously it was [w, x, y, z].
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:126:- **[api rename]** Starting with **v0.4.5**, `glm_simd_` functions are renamed to `glmm_`.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:127:- **[new option]** Starting with **v0.4.5**, alignment requirements can be disabled. Read more in the documentation.  
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:128:- **[major change]** Starting with **v0.5.0**, vec3 functions occupy the **glm_vec3_** namespace. This used to be **glm_vec_** in earlier versions.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:129:- **[major change]** Starting with **v0.5.1**, `vec3` and `mat3` types are not aligned by default.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:130:- **[major change]** Starting with **v0.7.3**, inline print functions are disabled by default in release mode to eliminate printing costs (see the Options chapter of the docs). <br> Colored output can be disabled (see documentation).
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:131:- **[major change]** Starting with **v0.8.3**, alternate clipspace configurations are supported. The `CGLM_FORCE_DEPTH_ZERO_TO_ONE` and `CGLM_FORCE_LEFT_HANDED` flags are provided to control clip depth and handedness. This makes it easier to incorporate cglm into projects using graphics APIs such as Vulkan or Metal. See https://cglm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/opt.html#clipspace-option-s
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:132:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:133:### 🚀 Features
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:134:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:135:- scalar and simd (sse, avx, neon...) optimizations
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:136:- general purpose matrix operations (mat4, mat3)
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:137:- chain matrix multiplication (square only)

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:162:        <div>Like other graphics libraries (especially OpenGL), cglm uses column-major layout to keep matrices in memory. </div>
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:163:        <div>&nbsp;</div>
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:164:        <div>While we might support row-major matrices in the future, currently if you need your matrices to be in row-major layout you have to transpose them. </div>
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:165:      </td>

src/third_party/cglm/README.md:174:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:175:cglm contains general purpose mat4 product and inverse functions but also provides optimized versions for affine transformations. If you want to multiply two affine transformation matrices you can use glm_mul instead of glm_mat4_mul and glm_inv_tr (ROT + TR) instead glm_mat4_inv.
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:176:```C
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:177:/* multiplication */
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:178:mat4 modelMat;
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:179:glm_mul(T, R, modelMat);
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:180:
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:181:/* othonormal rot + tr matrix inverse (rigid-body) */
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:182:glm_inv_tr(modelMat);
src/third_party/cglm/README.md:183:```

src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:1:# CONTRIBUTING
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:2:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:3:Any contributions (code, documentation, ...) are welcome.
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:4:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:5:# New Features
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:6:- This library may not accept all new features, it is better to create an issue and get approval before coding
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:7:- You must add test for every new feature
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:8:- The feature must be compiled on both UNIX/POSIX systems (e.g. macos, linux...) and Windows
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:9:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:10:# Code Style
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:11:This library is written with C99, don't try to add C++ files (yes it can compiled into lib),
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:12:if you have enough reason to add C++ files than create an issue and get approval before coding,
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:13:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:14:- All functions must have `glm` prefix
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:15:- Lines should be wrapped at 80 characters.
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:16:- Don't invent new style for existing ones
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:17:- Use C89 style comments (`/* comments */`) not C++ style comments (`// comments`)
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:18:- Don't use TABs instead use 2 spaces for TABs
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:19:- All indents must be 2 spaces, not 1 nor 4 space
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:20:- All functions in `include` folder must be exported by `CGLM_EXPORT` and wrapped by `extern "C" {` for C++
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:21:- Crate new line for return type, attribs:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:22:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:23:```C
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:24:CGLM_INLINE
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:25:void
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:26:glm_mul(mat4 m1, mat4 m2, mat4 dest)
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:27:```
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:28:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:29:not acceptable:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:30:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:31:```C
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:32:CGLM_INLINE void glm_mul(mat4 m1, mat4 m2, mat4 dest)
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:33:```
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:34:- Variables must be declared at the top of a scope before usage:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:35:```C
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:36:int x;
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:37:int y;
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:38:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:39:x = y = 0;
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:40:```
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:41:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:42:not acceptable:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:43:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:44:```C
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:45:int x;
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:46:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:47:x = 0;
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:48:int y = 0;
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:49:```
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:50:
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:51:- All files must retain same LICENSE statement
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:52:- Code with warnings will not be accepted, please suppress them (not by disabling them)
src/third_party/cglm/CONTRIBUTING.md:53:- Run code anaylysis before submitting pull requests, if you use Xcode you can enable Sanitizer in scheme, you can use valgrind in linux

src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:51:
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:52:  glm_vec3_sub(v1, v0, edge1);

src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:65:  if (u < 0.0f || u > 1.0f)
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:66:    return false;
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:67:

src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:75:

src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:78:
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:79:  return dist > epsilon;

src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:83: * @brief ray sphere intersection
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:84: *
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:85: * returns false if there is no intersection if true:
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:86: *
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:87: * - t1 > 0, t2 > 0: ray intersects the sphere at t1 and t2 both ahead of the origin

src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:91: *   specific range (for example, tmin < t1, t2 < tmax) to determine if the
src/third_party/cglm/include/cglm/ray.h:92: *   intersections are within a desired segment of the ray

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:1:.. default-domain:: C
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:2:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:3:3D Affine Transform Matrix (specialized functions)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:4:================================================================================
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:5:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:6:Header: cglm/affine-mat.h
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:7:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:8:We mostly use glm_mat4_* for 4x4 general and transform matrices. **cglm**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:9:provides optimized version of some functions. Because affine transform matrix is
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:10:a known format, for instance all last item of first three columns is zero.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:11:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:12:You should be careful when using these functions. For instance :c:func:`glm_mul`
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:13:assumes matrix will be this format:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:14:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:15:.. code-block:: text
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:16:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:17:   R  R  R  X
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:18:   R  R  R  Y
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:19:   R  R  R  Z
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:20:   0  0  0  W
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:21:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:22:if you override zero values here then use :c:func:`glm_mat4_mul` version.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:23:You cannot use :c:func:`glm_mul` anymore.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:24:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:25:Same is also true for :c:func:`glm_inv_tr` if you only have rotation and
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:26:translation then it will work as expected, otherwise you cannot use that.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:27:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:28:In the future it may accept scale factors too but currently it does not.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:29:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:30:Table of contents (click func go):
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:31:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:42:.. c:function:: void  glm_mul(mat4 m1, mat4 m2, mat4 dest)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:43:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:44:    | this is similar to glm_mat4_mul but specialized to affine transform
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:45:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:46:    Matrix format should be:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:47:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:48:    .. code-block:: text
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:49:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:50:       R  R  R  X
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:51:       R  R  R  Y
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:52:       R  R  R  Z
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:53:       0  0  0  W
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:54:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:55:    this reduces some multiplications. It should be faster than mat4_mul.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:56:    if you are not sure about matrix format then DON'T use this! use mat4_mul
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:57:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:58:    Parameters:

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:65:    | this is similar to glm_mat4_mul but specialized to rotation matrix
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:66:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:67:    Right Matrix format should be (left is free):
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:68:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:69:    .. code-block:: text
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:70:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:71:       R  R  R  0
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:72:       R  R  R  0
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:73:       R  R  R  0
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:74:       0  0  0  1
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:75:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:76:    this reduces some multiplications. It should be faster than mat4_mul.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:77:    if you are not sure about matrix format then DON'T use this! use mat4_mul
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:78:

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:84:.. c:function:: void  glm_inv_tr(mat4 mat)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:85:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:86:    | inverse orthonormal rotation + translation matrix (ridig-body)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:87:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:88:    .. code-block:: text
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:89:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:90:       X = | R  T |   X' = | R' -R'T |
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:91:           | 0  1 |        | 0     1 |
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:92:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:93:    use this if you only have rotation + translation, this should work faster
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:94:    than :c:func:`glm_mat4_inv`
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:95:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine-mat.rst:96:    Don't use this if your matrix includes other things e.g. scale, shear...

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:1:.. default-domain:: C
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:2:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:3:euler angles
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:4:============
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:5:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:6:Header: cglm/euler.h
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:7:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:8:You may wonder what **glm_euler_sq** type ( **_sq** stands for sequence ) and
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:9::c:func:`glm_euler_by_order` do.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:10:I used them to convert euler angles in one coordinate system to another. For
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:11:instance if you have **Z_UP** euler angles and if you want to convert it
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:12:to **Y_UP** axis then :c:func:`glm_euler_by_order` is your friend. For more
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:13:information check :c:func:`glm_euler_order` documentation
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:14:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:15:You must pass arrays as array, if you use C compiler then you can use something
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:16:like this:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:17:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:18:.. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:19:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:20:   float pitch, yaw, roll;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:21:   mat4  rot;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:22:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:23:   /* pitch = ...; yaw = ...; roll = ... */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:24:   glm_euler((vec3){pitch, yaw, roll}, rot);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:25:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:26:Rotation Conveniention
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:27:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:28:Current *cglm*'s euler functions uses these convention:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:29:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:30:* Tait–Bryan angles (x-y-z convention)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:31:* Intrinsic rotations (pitch, yaw and roll).
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:32:  This is reserve order of extrinsic (elevation, heading and bank) rotation
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:33:* Right hand rule (actually all rotations in *cglm* use **RH**)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:34:* All angles used in *cglm* are **RADIANS** not degrees
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:35:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:36:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:37:**NOTE**: The default :c:func:`glm_euler` function is the short name of
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:38::c:func:`glm_euler_xyz` this is why you can't see :c:func:`glm_euler_xyz`.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:39:When you see an euler function which doesn't have any X, Y, Z suffix then
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:40:assume that uses **_xyz** (or instead it accept order as parameter).
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:41:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:42:If rotation doesn't work properly, your options:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:43:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:44:1. If you use (or paste) degrees convert it to radians before calling an euler function
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:45:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:46:.. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:47:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:48:   float pitch, yaw, roll;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:49:   mat4  rot;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:50:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:51:   /* pitch = degrees; yaw = degrees; roll = degrees */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:52:   glm_euler((vec3){glm_rad(pitch), glm_rad(yaw), glm_rad(roll)}, rot);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:53:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:54:2. Convention mismatch. You may have extrinsic angles,
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:55:   if you do (if you must) then consider to use reverse order e.g if you have
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:56:   **xyz** extrinsic then use **zyx**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:57:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:58:3. *cglm* may implemented it wrong, consider to create an issue to report it
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:59:   or pull request to fix it
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:60:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:61:Table of contents (click to go):

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:84:.. c:function:: glm_euler_sq  glm_euler_order(int ord[3])
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:85:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:86:    | packs euler angles order to glm_euler_sq enum.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:87:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:88:    To use :c:func:`glm_euler_by_order` function you need *glm_euler_sq*. You
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:89:    can get it with this function.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:90:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:91:    You can build param like this:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:92:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:93:    | X = 0, Y = 1, Z = 2
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:94:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:95:    if you have ZYX order then you pass this: [2, 1, 0] = ZYX.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:96:    if you have YXZ order then you pass this: [1, 0, 2] = YXZ
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:97:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:98:    As you can see first item specifies which axis will be first then the
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:99:    second one specifies which one will be next an so on.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:100:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:101:    Parameters:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:102:      | *[in]*  **ord**  euler angles order [Angle1, Angle2, Angle2]
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:103:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:104:    Returns:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:105:      packed euler order
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:106:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:107:.. c:function:: void  glm_euler_angles(mat4 m, vec3 dest)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:108:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/euler.rst:109:    | extract euler angles (in radians) using xyz order

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:1:Struct API 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:2:================================
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:3:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:4:Struct API is alternative API to array api to use **cglm** with improved type safety and easy to use. 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:5:Since struct api is built top of array api, every struct API is not documented here. 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:6:See array api documentation for more information for individual functions.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:7:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:8:By default struct api adds `s` suffix to every type name e.g. vec3s, mat4s, versors etc. 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:9:Also struct api `s` suffix to namespace e.g. `glms_vec3_add`, `glms_mat4_mul` etc.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:10:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:11:By starting v0.9.0, struct api namespace is configurable. We can omit **glms_** namespace or 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:12:even change it with custom name to move existing api integrations to **cglm** more easily...
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:13:We can also add **s** to function names if we want e.g. `glms_vec3_add()` -> `vec3_add()` or `vec3s_add()`.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:14:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:15:By including **cglm/struct.h** header you will include all struct api. It will also include **cglm/cglm.h** too. 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:16:Since struct apis are inline you don't need to build or link *cglm* against 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:17:your project unless if you want to use pre-built call-api too.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:18:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:19:Struct API is built top of array api. So you can mix them. 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:20:Use **.raw** union member to access raw array data to use it with array api. 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:21:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:22:Unlike array api ([0], [1], [0][0] ...), it is also possible to use struct api 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:23:with **.x**, **.y**, **.z**, **.w**, **.r**, **.g**, **.b**, **.a**, **.m00**, **m01**... 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:24:accessors to access individual elements/properties of vectors and matrices.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:25:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:26:Struct API usage:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:27:-----------------
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:28:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:29:.. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:30:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:31:   #include <cglm/struct.h>
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:32:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:33:   mat4s m1  = glms_mat4_identity(); /* init...  */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:34:   mat4s m2  = glms_mat4_identity(); /* init...  */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:35:   mat4s m3  = glms_mat4_mul(glms_mat4_mul(m1, m2), glms_mat4_mul(m3, m4));
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:36:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:37:   vec3s v1  = { 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:38:   vec3s v2  = { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:39:   vec4s v4  = { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:40:   vec4  v5a = { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:41:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:42:   mat4s m4 = glms_rotate(m3, M_PI_2, 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:43:                          glms_vec3_cross(glms_vec3_add(v1, v6) 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:44:                                          glms_vec3_add(v1, v7)));
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:45:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:46:   v1.x = 1.0f; v1.y = 0.0f; v1.z = 0.0f;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:47:   // or
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:48:   v1.raw[0] = 1.0f; v1.raw[1] = 0.0f; v1.raw[2] = 0.0f;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:49:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:50:   /* use struct api with array api (mix them). */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:51:   /* use .raw to access array and use it with array api */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:52:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:53:   glm_vec4_add(m4.col[0].raw, v5a, m4.col[0].raw);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:54:   glm_mat4_mulv(m4.raw, v4.raw, v5a);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:55:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:56:or omit `glms_` namespace completely (see options below):
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:57:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:58:.. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:59:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:60:   #define CGLM_OMIT_NS_FROM_STRUCT_API
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:61:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:62:   #include <cglm/struct.h>
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:63:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:64:   mat4s m1  = mat4_identity(); /* init...  */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:65:   mat4s m2  = mat4_identity(); /* init...  */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:66:   mat4s m3  = mat4_mul(mat4_mul(m1, m2), mat4_mul(m3, m4));
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:67:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:68:   vec3s v1  = { 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:69:   vec3s v2  = { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:70:   vec4s v4  = { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:71:   vec4  v5a = { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:72:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:73:   mat4s m4 = glms_rotate(m3, M_PI_2, 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:74:                          vec3_cross(vec3_add(v1, v6) 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:75:                                     vec3_add(v1, v7)));
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:76:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:77:   v1.x = 1.0f; v1.y = 0.0f; v1.z = 0.0f;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:78:   // or
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:79:   v1.raw[0] = 1.0f; v1.raw[1] = 0.0f; v1.raw[2] = 0.0f;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:80:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:81:   /* use struct api with array api (mix them) */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:82:   glm_vec4_add(m4.col[0].raw, v5a, m4.col[0].raw);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:83:   glm_mat4_mulv(m4.raw, v4.raw, v5a);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:84:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:85:Configuring the Struct API:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:86:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:87:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:88:To configure the Struct API namespace, you can define the following macros before including the cglm/struct.h header:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:89:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:90:- **CGLM_OMIT_NS_FROM_STRUCT_API**: omits CGLM_STRUCT_API_NS (`glms_`) namespace completely if there is sub namespace e.g `mat4_`, `vec4_` ... DEFAULT is not defined
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:91:- **CGLM_STRUCT_API_NS**:           define name space for struct api, DEFAULT is **glms**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:92:- **CGLM_STRUCT_API_NAME_SUFFIX**:  define name suffix, DEFAULT is **empty** e.g defining it as #define CGLM_STRUCT_API_NAME_SUFFIX  s will add s suffix to mat4_mul -> mat4s_mul
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:93:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:94:❗️ IMPORTANT ❗️
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:95:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:96:It's a good idea to set up your config macros in build settings like CMake, Xcode, or Visual Studio. This is especially important if you're using features like Modules in Xcode, where adding macros directly before the **cglm** headers might not work.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:97:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_struct.rst:98:Detailed documentation for Struct API:

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:22:.. c:function:: bool  glm_ray_triangle(vec3 origin, vec3 direction, vec3 v0, vec3 v1, vec3 v2, float *d)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:23:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:24:    Möller–Trumbore ray-triangle intersection algorithm
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:25:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:26:    Parameters:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:27:      | *[in]*       **origin**        origin of ray
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:28:      | *[in]*       **direction**     direction of ray
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:29:      | *[in]*       **v0**            first vertex of triangle
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:30:      | *[in]*       **v1**            second vertex of triangle
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:31:      | *[in]*       **v2**            third vertex of triangle
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:32:      | *[in, out]*  **d**             float pointer to save distance to intersection
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:33:      | *[out]*      **intersection**  whether there is intersection
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:34:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:35:.. c:function:: bool glm_ray_sphere(vec3 origin, vec3 dir, vec4 s, float * __restrict t1, float * __restrict t2)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:36:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:37:    ray sphere intersection
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:38:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:39:    returns false if there is no intersection if true:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:40:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:41:    - t1 > 0, t2 > 0: ray intersects the sphere at t1 and t2 both ahead of the origin
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:42:    - t1 < 0, t2 > 0: ray starts inside the sphere, exits at t2
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:43:    - t1 < 0, t2 < 0: no intersection ahead of the ray ( returns false )
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:44:    - the caller can check if the intersection points (t1 and t2) fall within a
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:45:      specific range (for example, tmin < t1, t2 < tmax) to determine if the
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:46:      intersections are within a desired segment of the ray
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:47:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:48:    Parameters:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:49:      | *[in]*   **origin**  ray origin
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:50:      | *[in]*   **dir**     normalized ray direction
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:51:      | *[in]*   **s**       sphere  [center.x, center.y, center.z, radii]
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:52:      | *[out]*  **t1**      near point1 (closer to origin)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/ray.rst:53:      | *[out]*  **t2**      far point2 (farther from origin)

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:3:camera
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:4:======
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:5:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:6:Header: cglm/cam.h
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:7:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:8:There are many convenient functions for camera. For instance :c:func:`glm_look`
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:9:is just wrapper for :c:func:`glm_lookat`. Sometimes you only have direction
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:10:instead of target, so that makes easy to build view matrix using direction.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:11:There is also :c:func:`glm_look_anyup` function which can help build view matrix
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:12:without providing UP axis. It uses :c:func:`glm_vec3_ortho` to get a UP axis and
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:13:builds view matrix.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:14:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:15:You can also *_default* versions of ortho and perspective to build projection
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:16:fast if you don't care specific projection values.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:17:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:18:*_decomp* means decompose; these function can help to decompose projection
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:19:matrices.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:20:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:21:.. note:: Be careful when working with high range (very small near, very large
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:22:   far) projection matrices. You may not get exact value you gave.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:23:   **float** type cannot store very high precision so you will lose precision.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:24:   Also your projection matrix will be inaccurate due to losing precision
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:25:

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:157:    such as shadow volumes. Dispatches to the appropriate clipspace variant
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/cam.rst:158:    based on compile-time configuration (LH/RH, NO/ZO).

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:3:frustum
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:4:=============
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:5:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:6:Header: cglm/frustum.h
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:7:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:8:cglm provides convenient functions to extract frustum planes, corners...
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:9:All extracted corners are **vec4** so you must create array of **vec4**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:10:not **vec3**. If you want to store them to save space you msut convert them
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:11:yourself.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:12:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:13:**vec4** is used to speed up functions need to corners. This is why frustum
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:14:functions use *vec4* instead of *vec3*
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:15:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:16:Currently related-functions use [-1, 1] clip space configuration to extract
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:17:corners but you can override it by prodiving **GLM_CUSTOM_CLIPSPACE** macro.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:18:If you provide it then you have to all bottom macros as *vec4*
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:19:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:20:Current configuration:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:21:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:22:.. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:23:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:24:   /* near */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:25:   GLM_CSCOORD_LBN {-1.0f, -1.0f, -1.0f, 1.0f}
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:26:   GLM_CSCOORD_LTN {-1.0f,  1.0f, -1.0f, 1.0f}
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:27:   GLM_CSCOORD_RTN { 1.0f,  1.0f, -1.0f, 1.0f}
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:28:   GLM_CSCOORD_RBN { 1.0f, -1.0f, -1.0f, 1.0f}
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:29:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:30:   /* far */
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:31:   GLM_CSCOORD_LBF {-1.0f, -1.0f,  1.0f, 1.0f}
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:32:   GLM_CSCOORD_LTF {-1.0f,  1.0f,  1.0f, 1.0f}
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:33:   GLM_CSCOORD_RTF { 1.0f,  1.0f,  1.0f, 1.0f}
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:34:   GLM_CSCOORD_RBF { 1.0f, -1.0f,  1.0f, 1.0f}

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:82:.. c:function:: void  glm_frustum_planes(mat4 m, vec4 dest[6])
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:83:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:84:    | extracts view frustum planes
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:85:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:86:    planes' space:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:87:     - if m = proj:     View Space
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:88:     - if m = viewProj: World Space
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:89:     - if m = MVP:      Object Space
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:90:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:91:    You probably want to extract planes in world space so use viewProj as m
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:92:    Computing viewProj:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:93:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:94:    .. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:95:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:96:       glm_mat4_mul(proj, view, viewProj);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:97:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:98:    Exracted planes order: [left, right, bottom, top, near, far]
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:99:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:100:    Parameters:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:101:      | *[in]*  **m**     matrix
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:102:      | *[out]* **dest**  exracted view frustum planes
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:103:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:104:.. c:function:: void  glm_frustum_corners(mat4 invMat, vec4 dest[8])
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:105:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:106:    | extracts view frustum corners using clip-space coordinates
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:107:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:108:    corners' space:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:109:     - if m = invViewProj: World Space
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:110:     - if m = invMVP:      Object Space
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:111:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:112:    You probably want to extract corners in world space so use **invViewProj**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:113:    Computing invViewProj:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:114:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:115:    .. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:116:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:117:       glm_mat4_mul(proj, view, viewProj);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:118:       ...
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:119:       glm_mat4_inv(viewProj, invViewProj);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:120:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:121:    if you have a near coord at **i** index,
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:122:    you can get it's far coord by i + 4;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:123:    follow example below to understand that
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:124:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:125:    For instance to find center coordinates between a near and its far coord:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:126:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:127:    .. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:128:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:129:       for (j = 0; j < 4; j++) {
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:130:         glm_vec3_center(corners[i], corners[i + 4], centerCorners[i]);
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:131:       }
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:132:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:133:    corners[i + 4] is far of corners[i] point.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:134:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:135:    Parameters:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:136:      | *[in]*  **invMat** matrix
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:137:      | *[out]* **dest**   exracted view frustum corners
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:138:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/frustum.rst:139:.. c:function:: void  glm_frustum_center(vec4 corners[8], vec4 dest)

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:1:Getting Started
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:2:================================
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:3:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:4:Types:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:5:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:6:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:7:**cglm** uses **glm** prefix for all functions e.g. glm_lookat. You can see supported types in common header file:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:8:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:9:.. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:10:  :linenos:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:11:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:12:  typedef float                   vec2[2];
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:13:  typedef float                   vec3[3];
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:14:  typedef int                    ivec3[3];
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:15:  typedef CGLM_ALIGN_IF(16) float vec4[4];
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:16:  typedef vec4                    versor;
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:17:  typedef vec3                    mat3[3];
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:18:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:19:  #ifdef __AVX__
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:20:  typedef CGLM_ALIGN_IF(32) vec4  mat4[4];
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:21:  #else
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:22:  typedef CGLM_ALIGN_IF(16) vec4  mat4[4];
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:23:  #endif
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:24:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:25:As you can see types don't store extra information in favor of space.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:26:You can send these values e.g. matrix to OpenGL directly without casting or calling a function like *value_ptr*
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:27:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:28:Alignment Is Required:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:29:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:30:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:31:**vec4** and **mat4** requires 16 (32 for **mat4** if AVX is enabled) byte alignment because **vec4** and **mat4** operations are vectorized by SIMD instructions (SSE/AVX/NEON).
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:32:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:33:**UPDATE:**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:34:  By starting v0.4.5 cglm provides an option to disable alignment requirement, it is enabled as default
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:35:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:36:  | Check :doc:`opt` page for more details
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:37:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:38:  Also alignment is disabled for older msvc versions as default. Now alignment is only required in Visual Studio 2017 version 15.6+ if CGLM_ALL_UNALIGNED macro is not defined.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:39:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:40:Allocations:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:41:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:42:*cglm* doesn't alloc any memory on heap. So it doesn't provide any allocator.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:43:You must allocate memory yourself. You should alloc memory for out parameters too if you pass pointer of memory location. When allocating memory, don't forget that **vec4** and **mat4** require alignment.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:44:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:45:.. note:: Unaligned **vec4** and unaligned **mat4** operations will be supported in the future. Check todo list.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:46:   Because you may want to multiply a CGLM matrix with external matrix.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:47:   There is no guarantee that non-CGLM matrix is aligned. Unaligned types will have *u* prefix e.g. **umat4**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:48:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:49:Array vs Struct:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:50:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:51:*cglm* uses arrays for vector and matrix types. So you can't access individual
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:52:elements like vec.x, vec.y, vec.z... You must use subscript to access vector elements
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:53:e.g. vec[0], vec[1], vec[2].
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:54:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:55:Also I think it is more meaningful to access matrix elements with subscript
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:56:e.g **matrix[2][3]** instead of **matrix._23**. Since matrix is array of vectors,
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:57:vectors are also defined as array. This makes types homogeneous.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:58:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:59:**Return arrays?**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:60:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:61:Since C doesn't support return arrays, cglm also doesn't support this feature.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:62:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:63:Function design:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:64:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:65:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:66:.. image:: cglm-intro.png
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:67:   :width: 492px 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:68:   :height: 297px
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:69:   :align: center
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:70:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:71:cglm provides a few way to call a function to do same operation.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:72:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:73:* Inline - *glm_, glm_u*
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:74:* Pre-compiled - *glmc_, glmc_u*
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:75:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:76:For instance **glm_mat4_mul** is inline (all *glm_* functions are inline), to make it non-inline (pre-compiled),
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:77:call it as **glmc_mat4_mul** from library, to use unaligned version use **glm_umat4_mul** (todo).
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:78:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:79:Most functions have **dest** parameter for output. For instance mat4_mul func looks like this:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:80:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:81:.. code-block:: c
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:82:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:83:   CGLM_INLINE
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:84:   void
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:85:   glm_mat4_mul(mat4 m1, mat4 m2, mat4 dest)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:86:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:87:The dest parameter is out parameter. Result will be stored in **dest**.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:88:Also in this case matrix multiplication order is dest = m1 * m2.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:89:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:90:* Changing parameter order will change the multiplication order.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:91:* You can pass all parameter same (this is similar to m1 `*=` m1), you can pass **dest** as m1 or m2 (this is similar to m1 `*=` m2)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:92:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:93:**v** postfix in function names
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:94:-------------------------------
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:95:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:96:You may see **v** postfix in some function names, v stands for vector.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:97:For instance consider a function that accepts three parameters x, y, z.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:98:This function may be overloaded by **v** postfix to accept vector (vec3) instead of separate parameters.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:99:In some places the v means that it will be apply to a vector.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:100:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:101:**_to** postfix in function names
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:102:---------------------------------
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:103:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:104:*_to* version of function will store the result in specified parameter instead of in-out parameter.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/getting_started.rst:105:Some functions don't have _to prefix but they still behave like this e.g. glm_mat4_mul.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:1:.. default-domain:: C
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:2:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:3:version
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:4:================================================================================
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:5:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:6:Header: cglm/version.h
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:7:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:8:**cglm** uses semantic versioning (http://semver.org) which is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:9:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:10:| **CGLM_VERSION_MAJOR** is major number of the version.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:11:| **CGLM_VERSION_MINOR** is minor number of the version.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:12:| **CGLM_VERSION_PATCH** is patch number of the version.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:13:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:14:every release increases these numbers. You can check existing version by 
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/version.rst:15:including `cglm/version.h`

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_simd.rst:2:================================
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_simd.rst:3:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_simd.rst:4:SIMD api is special api for SIMD operations. **glmm_** prefix is used for SIMD operations in cglm. It is used in many places in cglm.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/api_simd.rst:5:You can use it for your own SIMD operations too. In the future the api may be extended by time.

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:10:Initialize Transform Matrices
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:11:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:12:Functions with **_make** prefix expect you don't have a matrix and they create
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:13:a matrix for you. You don't need to pass identity matrix.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:14:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:15:But other functions expect you have a matrix and you want to transform them. If
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:16:you didn't have any existing matrix you have to initialize matrix to identity
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/affine2d.rst:17:before sending to transform functions.

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:7:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:8:Some convenient functions provided for AABB.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:9:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:10:**Definition of box:**
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:11:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:12:cglm defines box as two dimensional array of vec3.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:13:The first element is **min** point and the second one is **max** point.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:14:If you have another type e.g. struct or even another representation then you must
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/box.rst:15:convert it before and after call cglm box function.

src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:430:.. c:function:: bool glm_vec4_reflect(vec4 v, vec4 n, vec4 dest)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:431:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:432:    Reflection vector using an incident ray and a surface normal
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:433:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:434:    Parameters:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:435:      | *[in]*  **v**     incident vector
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:436:      | *[in]*  **n**     *❗️ normalized ❗️* normal vector
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:437:      | *[out]* **dest**  destination: reflection result
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:438:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:439:.. c:function:: bool glm_vec4_refract(vec4 v, vec4 n, float eta, vec4 dest)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:440:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:441:    computes refraction vector for an incident vector and a surface normal.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:442:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:443:    Calculates the refraction vector based on Snell's law. If total internal reflection
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:444:    occurs (angle too great given eta), dest is set to zero and returns false.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:445:    Otherwise, computes refraction vector, stores it in dest, and returns true.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:446:   
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:447:    This implementation does not explicitly preserve the 'w' component of the
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:448:    incident vector 'I' in the output 'dest', users requiring the preservation of
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:449:    the 'w' component should manually adjust 'dest' after calling this function.
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:450:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:451:    Parameters:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:452:      | *[in]*  **v**     *❗️ normalized ❗️* incident vector
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:453:      | *[in]*  **n**     *❗️ normalized ❗️* normal vector
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:454:      | *[in]*  **eta**   ratio of indices of refraction (incident/transmitted)
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:455:      | *[out]* **dest**  refraction vector if refraction occurs; zero vector otherwise
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:456:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:457:    Returns:
src/third_party/cglm/docs/source/vec4.rst:458:      returns true if refraction occurs; false if total internal reflection occurs.
