src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17265:\page faq Frequently asked questions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17266:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17267:<b>What is VMA?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17268:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17269:Vulkan(R) Memory Allocator (VMA) is a software library for developers who use the Vulkan graphics API in their code.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17270:It is written in C++.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17271:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17272:<b>What is the license of VMA?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17273:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17274:VMA is licensed under MIT, which means it is open source and free software.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17275:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17276:<b>What is the purpose of VMA?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17277:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17278:VMA helps with handling one aspect of Vulkan usage, which is device memory management -
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17279:allocation of `VkDeviceMemory` objects, and creation of `VkBuffer` and `VkImage` objects.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17280:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17281:<b>Do I need to use VMA?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17282:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17283:You don't need to, but it may be beneficial in many cases.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17284:Vulkan is a complex and low-level API, so libraries like this that abstract certain aspects of the API
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17285:and bring them to a higher level are useful.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17286:When developing any non-trivial Vulkan application, you likely need to use a memory allocator.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17287:Using VMA can save time compared to implementing your own.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17288:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17289:<b>When should I not use VMA?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17290:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17291:While VMA is useful for most applications that use the Vulkan API, there are cases
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17292:when it may be a better choice not to use it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17293:For example, if the application is very simple, e.g. serving as a sample or a learning exercise
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17294:to help you understand or teach others the basics of Vulkan,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17295:and it creates only a small number of buffers and images, then including VMA may be an overkill.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17296:Developing your own memory allocator may also be a good learning exercise.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17297:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17298:<b>What are the benefits of using VMA?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17299:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17300:-# VMA helps in choosing the optimal memory type for your resource (buffer or image).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17301:   In Vulkan, we have a two-level hierarchy of memory heaps and types with different flags,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17302:   and each device can expose a different set of those.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17303:   Implementing logic that would select the best memory type on each platform is a non-trivial task.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17304:   VMA does that, expecting only a high-level description of the intended usage of your resource.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17305:   For more information, see \subpage choosing_memory_type.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17306:-# VMA allocates large blocks of `VkDeviceMemory` and sub-allocates parts of them for your resources.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17307:   Allocating a new block of device memory may be a time-consuming operation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17308:   Some platforms also have a limit on the maximum number of those blocks (`VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::maxMemoryAllocationCount`)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17309:   as low as 4096, so allocating a separate one for each resource is not an option.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17310:   Sub-allocating parts of a memory block requires implementing an allocation algorithm,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17311:   which is a non-trivial task.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17312:   VMA does that, using an advanced and efficient algorithm that works well in various use cases.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17313:-# VMA offers a simple API that allows creating buffers and textures within one function call.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17314:   In Vulkan, the creation of a resource is a multi-step process.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17315:   You need to create a `VkBuffer` or `VkImage`, ask it for memory requirements,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17316:   allocate a `VkDeviceMemory` object, and finally bind the resource to the memory block.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17317:   VMA does that automatically under a simple API within one function call: vmaCreateBuffer(), vmaCreateImage().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17318:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17319:The library is doing much more under the hood.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17320:For example, it respects limits like `bufferImageGranularity`, `nonCoherentAtomSize`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17321:and `VkMemoryDedicatedRequirements` automatically, so you don't need to think about it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17322:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17323:<b>Which version should I pick?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17324:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17325:You can just pick [the latest version from the "master" branch](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17326:It is kept in a good shape most of the time, compiling and working correctly,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17327:with no compatibility-breaking changes and no unfinished code.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17328:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17329:If you want an even more stable version, you can pick
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17330:[the latest official release](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator/releases).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17331:Current code from the master branch is occasionally tagged as a release,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17332:with [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17333:carefully curated to enumerate all important changes since the previous version.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17334:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17335:The library uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17336:which means versions that only differ in the patch number are forward and backward compatible
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17337:(e.g., only fixing some bugs), while versions that differ in the minor number are backward compatible
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17338:(e.g., only adding new functions to the API, but not removing or changing existing ones).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17339:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17340:<b>How to integrate it with my code?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17341:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17342:VMA is an STB-style single-header C++ library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17343:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17344:You can pull the entire GitHub repository, e.g. using Git submodules.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17345:The repository contains ancillary files like the Cmake script, Doxygen config file,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17346:sample application, test suite, and others.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17347:You can compile it as a library and link with your project.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17348:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17349:However, a simpler way is taking the single file "include/vk_mem_alloc.h" and including it in your project.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17350:This extensive file contains all you need: a copyright notice,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17351:declarations of the public library interface (API), its internal implementation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17352:and even the documentation in form of Doxygen-style comments.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17353:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17354:The "STB style" means not everything is implemented as inline functions in the header file.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17355:You need to extract the internal implementation using a special macro.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17356:This means that in every .cpp file where you need to use the library you should
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17357:`#include "vk_mem_alloc.h"` to include its public interface,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17358:but additionally in exactly one .cpp file you should `#define VMA_IMPLEMENTATION`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17359:before this `#include` to enable its internal implementation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17360:For more information, see [Project setup](@ref quick_start_project_setup).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17361:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17362:<b>Does the library work with C or C++?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17363:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17364:The internal implementation of VMA is written in C++.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17365:It is distributed in the source format, so you need a compiler supporting at least C++14 to build it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17366:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17367:However, the public interface of the library is written in C - using only enums, structs, and global functions,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17368:in the same style as Vulkan, so you can use the library in the C code.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17369:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17370:<b>I am not a fan of modern C++. Can I still use it?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17371:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17372:Very likely yes.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17373:We acknowledge that many C++ developers, especially in the games industry,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17374:do not appreciate all the latest features that the language has to offer.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17375:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17376:- VMA doesn't throw or catch any C++ exceptions.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17377:  It reports errors by returning a `VkResult` value instead, just like Vulkan.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17378:  If you don't use exceptions in your project, your code is not exception-safe,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17379:  or even if you disable exception handling in the compiler options, you can still use VMA.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17380:- VMA doesn't use C++ run-time type information like `typeid` or `dynamic_cast`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17381:  so if you disable RTTI in the compiler options, you can still use the library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17382:- VMA uses only a limited subset of standard C and C++ library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17383:  It doesn't use STL containers like `std::vector`, `map`, or `string`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17384:  either in the public interface nor in the internal implementation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17385:  It implements its own containers instead.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17386:- If you don't use the default heap memory allocator through `malloc/free` or `new/delete`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17387:  but implement your own allocator instead, you can pass it to VMA and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17388:  the library will use your functions for every dynamic heap allocation made internally,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17389:  as well as passing it further to Vulkan functions. For details, see [Custom host memory allocator](@ref custom_memory_allocator).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17390:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17391:<b>Is it available for other programming languages?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17392:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17393:VMA is a C++ library with C interface in similar style as Vulkan.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17394:An object-oriented C++ wrapper or bindings to other programming languages are out of scope of this project,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17395:but they are welcome as external projects.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17396:Some of them are listed in [README.md, "See also" section](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator?tab=readme-ov-file#see-also),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17397:including binding to C++, Python, Rust, and Haskell.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17398:Before using any of them, please check if they are still maintained and updated to use a recent version of VMA.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17399:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17400:<b>What platforms does it support?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17401:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17402:VMA relies only on Vulkan and some parts of the standard C and C++ library,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17403:so it supports any platform where a C++ compiler and Vulkan are available.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17404:It is developed mostly on Microsoft(R) Windows(R),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17405:but it has been successfully used in Linux(R), MacOS, Android, and even FreeBSD and Raspberry Pi.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17406:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17407:<b>Does it only work on AMD GPUs?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17408:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17409:No! While VMA is published by AMD, it works on any GPU that supports Vulkan,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17410:whether a discrete PC graphics card, a processor integrated graphics, or a mobile SoC.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17411:It doesn't give AMD GPUs any advantage over any other GPUs.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17412:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17413:<b>What Vulkan versions and extensions are supported?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17414:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17415:VMA is updated to support the latest versions of Vulkan.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17416:It currently supports Vulkan up to 1.4.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17417:The library also supports older versions down to the first release of Vulkan 1.0.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17418:Defining a higher minimum version support would help simplify the code,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17419:but we acknowledge that developers on some platforms like Android still use older versions,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17420:so the support is provided for all of them.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17421:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17422:Among many extensions available for Vulkan, only a few interact with memory management.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17423:VMA can automatically take advantage of them. Some of them are:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17424:VK_EXT_memory_budget, VK_EXT_memory_priority, VK_KHR_external_memory_win32, and VK_KHR_maintenance*
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17425:extensions that are later promoted to the new versions of the core Vulkan API.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17426:To use them, it is your responsibility to validate if they are available on the current system and if so,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17427:enable them while creating the Vulkan device object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17428:You also need to pass appropriate #VmaAllocatorCreateFlagBits to inform VMA that they are enabled.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17429:Then, the library will automatically take advantage of them.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17430:For more information and the full list of supported extensions, see [Enabling extensions](@ref quick_start_initialization_enabling_extensions).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17431:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17432:<b>Does it support other graphics APIs, like Microsoft DirectX(R) 12?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17433:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17434:No, but we offer an equivalent library for DirectX 12:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17435:[D3D12 Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/D3D12MemoryAllocator).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17436:It uses the same core allocation algorithm.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17437:It also shares many features with VMA, like the support for custom pools and virtual allocator.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17438:However, it is not identical in terms of the features supported.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17439:Its API also looks different, because while the interface of VMA is similar in style to Vulkan,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17440:the interface of D3D12MA is similar to DirectX 12.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17441:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17442:<b>Is the library lightweight?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17443:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17444:It depends on how you define it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17445:VMA is implemented with high-performance and real-time applications like video games in mind.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17446:The CPU performance overhead of using this library is low.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17447:It uses a high-quality allocation algorithm called Two-Level Segregated Fit (TLSF),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17448:which in most cases can find a free place for a new allocation in few steps.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17449:The library also doesn't perform too many CPU heap allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17450:In many cases, the allocation happens with 0 new CPU heap allocations performed by the library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17451:Even the creation of a #VmaAllocation object doesn't typically feature an CPU allocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17452:because these objects are returned out of a dedicated memory pool.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17453:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17454:On the other hand, however, VMA needs some extra memory and extra time
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17455:to maintain the metadata about the occupied and free regions of the memory blocks,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17456:and the algorithms and data structures used must be generic enough to work well in most cases.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17457:If you develop your program for a very resource-constrained platform,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17458:a custom allocator simpler than VMA may be a better choice.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17459:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17460:<b>Does it have a documentation?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17461:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17462:Yes! VMA comes with full documentation of all elements of the API (functions, structures, enums),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17463:as well as many generic chapters that provide an introduction,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17464:describe core concepts of the library, good practices, etc.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17465:The entire documentation is written in form of code comments inside "vk_mem_alloc.h", in Doxygen format.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17466:You can access it in multiple ways:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17467:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17468:- Browsable online: https://gpuopen-librariesandsdks.github.io/VulkanMemoryAllocator/html/
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17469:- Local HTML pages available after you clone the repository and open file "docs/html/index.html".
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17470:- You can rebuild the documentation in HTML or some other format from the source code using Doxygen.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17471:  Configuration file "Doxyfile" is part of the repository.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17472:- Finally, you can just read the comments preceding declarations of any public functions of the library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17473:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17474:<b>Is it a mature project?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17475:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17476:Yes! The library is in development since June 2017, has over 1000 commits, over 500 issue tickets
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17477:and pull requests (most of them resolved), and over 80 contributors.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17478:It is distributed together with Vulkan SDK.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17479:It is used by many software projects, including some large and popular ones like Qt or Blender,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17480:as well as some AAA games.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17481:According to the [LunarG 2024 Ecosystem Survey](https://www.lunarg.com/2024-ecosystem-survey-progress-report-released/),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17482:it is used by over 50% of Vulkan developers.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17483:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17484:<b>How can I contribute to the project?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17485:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17486:If you have an idea for improvement or a feature request,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17487:you can go to [the library repository](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17488:and create an Issue ticket, describing your idea.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17489:You can also implement it yourself by forking the repository, making changes to the code,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17490:and creating a Pull request.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17491:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17492:If you want to ask a question, you can also create a ticket the same way.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17493:Before doing this, please make sure you read the relevant part of the Vulkan specification and VMA documentation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17494:where you may find the answers to your question.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17495:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17496:If you want to report a suspected bug, you can also create a ticket the same way.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17497:Before doing this, please put some effort into the investigation of whether the bug is really
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17498:in the library and not in your code or in the Vulkan implementation (the GPU driver) on your platform:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17499:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17500:- Enable Vulkan validation layer and make sure it is free from any errors.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17501:- Make sure `VMA_ASSERT` is defined to an implementation that can report a failure and not ignore it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17502:- Try making your allocation using pure Vulkan functions rather than VMA and see if the bug persists.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17503:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17504:<b>I found some compilation warnings. How can we fix them?</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17505:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17506:Seeing compiler warnings may be annoying to some developers,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17507:but it is a design decision to not fix all of them.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17508:Due to the nature of the C++ language, certain preprocessor macros can make some variables unused,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17509:function parameters unreferenced, or conditional expressions constant in some configurations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17510:The code of this library should not be bigger or more complicated just to silence these warnings.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17511:It is recommended to disable such warnings instead.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17512:For more information, see [Features not supported](@ref general_considerations_features_not_supported).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17513:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17514:However, if you observe a warning that is really dangerous, e.g.,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17515:about an implicit conversion from a larger to a smaller integer type, please report it and it will be fixed ASAP.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17516:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17517:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17518:\page quick_start Quick start
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17519:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17520:\section quick_start_project_setup Project setup
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17521:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17522:Vulkan Memory Allocator comes in form of a "stb-style" single header file.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17523:While you can pull the entire repository e.g. as Git module, there is also Cmake script provided,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17524:you don't need to build it as a separate library project.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17525:You can add file "vk_mem_alloc.h" directly to your project and submit it to code repository next to your other source files.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17526:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17527:"Single header" doesn't mean that everything is contained in C/C++ declarations,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17528:like it tends to be in case of inline functions or C++ templates.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17529:It means that implementation is bundled with interface in a single file and needs to be extracted using preprocessor macro.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17530:If you don't do it properly, it will result in linker errors.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17531:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17532:To do it properly:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17533:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17534:-# Include "vk_mem_alloc.h" file in each CPP file where you want to use the library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17535:   This includes declarations of all members of the library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17536:-# In exactly one CPP file define following macro before this include.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17537:   It enables also internal definitions.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17538:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17539:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17540:#define VMA_IMPLEMENTATION
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17541:#include "vk_mem_alloc.h"
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17542:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17543:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17544:It may be a good idea to create dedicated CPP file just for this purpose, e.g. "VmaUsage.cpp".
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17545:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17546:This library includes header `<vulkan/vulkan.h>`, which in turn
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17547:includes `<windows.h>` on Windows. If you need some specific macros defined
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17548:before including these headers (like `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` or
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17549:`WINVER` for Windows, `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR` for Vulkan), you must define
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17550:them before every `#include` of this library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17551:It may be a good idea to create a dedicate header file for this purpose, e.g. "VmaUsage.h",
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17552:that will be included in other source files instead of VMA header directly.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17553:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17554:This library is written in C++, but has C-compatible interface.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17555:Thus, you can include and use "vk_mem_alloc.h" in C or C++ code, but full
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17556:implementation with `VMA_IMPLEMENTATION` macro must be compiled as C++, NOT as C.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17557:Some features of C++14 are used and required. Features of C++20 are used optionally when available.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17558:Some headers of standard C and C++ library are used, but STL containers, RTTI, or C++ exceptions are not used.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17559:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17560:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17561:\section quick_start_initialization Initialization
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17562:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17563:VMA offers library interface in a style similar to Vulkan, with object handles like #VmaAllocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17564:structures describing parameters of objects to be created like #VmaAllocationCreateInfo,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17565:and errors codes returned from functions using `VkResult` type.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17566:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17567:The first and the main object that needs to be created is #VmaAllocator.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17568:It represents the initialization of the entire library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17569:Only one such object should be created per `VkDevice`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17570:You should create it at program startup, after `VkDevice` was created, and before any device memory allocator needs to be made.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17571:It must be destroyed before `VkDevice` is destroyed.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17572:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17573:At program startup:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17574:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17575:-# Initialize Vulkan to have `VkInstance`, `VkPhysicalDevice`, `VkDevice` object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17576:-# Fill VmaAllocatorCreateInfo structure and call vmaCreateAllocator() to create #VmaAllocator object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17577:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17578:Only members `physicalDevice`, `device`, `instance` are required.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17579:However, you should inform the library which Vulkan version do you use by setting
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17580:VmaAllocatorCreateInfo::vulkanApiVersion and which extensions did you enable
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17581:by setting VmaAllocatorCreateInfo::flags.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17582:Otherwise, VMA would use only features of Vulkan 1.0 core with no extensions.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17583:See below for details.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17584:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17585:\subsection quick_start_initialization_selecting_vulkan_version Selecting Vulkan version
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17586:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17587:VMA supports Vulkan version down to 1.0, for backward compatibility.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17588:If you want to use higher version, you need to inform the library about it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17589:This is a two-step process.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17590:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17591:<b>Step 1: Compile time.</b> By default, VMA compiles with code supporting the highest
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17592:Vulkan version found in the included `<vulkan/vulkan.h>` that is also supported by the library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17593:If this is OK, you don't need to do anything.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17594:However, if you want to compile VMA as if only some lower Vulkan version was available,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17595:define macro `VMA_VULKAN_VERSION` before every `#include "vk_mem_alloc.h"`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17596:It should have decimal numeric value in form of ABBBCCC, where A = major, BBB = minor, CCC = patch Vulkan version.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17597:For example, to compile against Vulkan 1.2:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17598:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17599:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17600:#define VMA_VULKAN_VERSION 1002000 // Vulkan 1.2
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17601:#include "vk_mem_alloc.h"
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17602:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17603:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17604:<b>Step 2: Runtime.</b> Even when compiled with higher Vulkan version available,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17605:VMA can use only features of a lower version, which is configurable during creation of the #VmaAllocator object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17606:By default, only Vulkan 1.0 is used.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17607:To initialize the allocator with support for higher Vulkan version, you need to set member
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17608:VmaAllocatorCreateInfo::vulkanApiVersion to an appropriate value, e.g. using constants like `VK_API_VERSION_1_2`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17609:See code sample below.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17610:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17611:\subsection quick_start_initialization_importing_vulkan_functions Importing Vulkan functions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17612:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17613:You may need to configure importing Vulkan functions. There are 4 ways to do this:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17614:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17615:-# **If you link with Vulkan static library** (e.g. "vulkan-1.lib" on Windows):
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17616:   - You don't need to do anything.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17617:   - VMA will use these, as macro `VMA_STATIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS` is defined to 1 by default.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17618:-# **If you want VMA to fetch pointers to Vulkan functions dynamically** using `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17619:   `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` (this is the option presented in the example below):
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17620:   - Define `VMA_STATIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS` to 0, `VMA_DYNAMIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS` to 1.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17621:   - Provide pointers to these two functions via VmaVulkanFunctions::vkGetInstanceProcAddr,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17622:     VmaVulkanFunctions::vkGetDeviceProcAddr.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17623:   - The library will fetch pointers to all other functions it needs internally.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17624:-# **If you fetch pointers to all Vulkan functions in a custom way**:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17625:   - Define `VMA_STATIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS` and `VMA_DYNAMIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS` to 0.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17626:   - Pass these pointers via structure #VmaVulkanFunctions.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17627:-# **If you use [volk library](https://github.com/zeux/volk)**:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17628:   - Define `VMA_STATIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS` and `VMA_DYNAMIC_VULKAN_FUNCTIONS` to 0.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17629:   - Use function vmaImportVulkanFunctionsFromVolk() to fill in the structure #VmaVulkanFunctions.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17630:     For more information, see the description of this function.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17631:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17632:\subsection quick_start_initialization_enabling_extensions Enabling extensions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17633:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17634:VMA can automatically use following Vulkan extensions.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17635:If you found them available on the selected physical device and you enabled them
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17636:while creating `VkInstance` / `VkDevice` object, inform VMA about their availability
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17637:by setting appropriate flags in VmaAllocatorCreateInfo::flags.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17638:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17639:Vulkan extension              | VMA flag
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17640:------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17641:VK_KHR_dedicated_allocation   | #VMA_ALLOCATOR_CREATE_KHR_DEDICATED_ALLOCATION_BIT
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17642:VK_KHR_bind_memory2           | #VMA_ALLOCATOR_CREATE_KHR_BIND_MEMORY2_BIT

src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17682:\subsection quick_start_initialization_other_config Other configuration options
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17683:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17684:There are additional configuration options available through preprocessor macros that you can define
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17685:before including VMA header and through parameters passed in #VmaAllocatorCreateInfo.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17686:They include a possibility to use your own callbacks for host memory allocations (`VkAllocationCallbacks`),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17687:callbacks for device memory allocations (instead of `vkAllocateMemory`, `vkFreeMemory`),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17688:or your custom `VMA_ASSERT` macro, among others.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17689:For more information, see: @ref configuration.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17690:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17691:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17692:\section quick_start_resource_allocation Resource allocation
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17693:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17694:When you want to create a buffer or image:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17695:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17696:-# Fill `VkBufferCreateInfo` / `VkImageCreateInfo` structure.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17697:-# Fill VmaAllocationCreateInfo structure.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17698:-# Call vmaCreateBuffer() / vmaCreateImage() to get `VkBuffer`/`VkImage` with memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17699:   already allocated and bound to it, plus #VmaAllocation objects that represents its underlying memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17700:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17701:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17702:VkBufferCreateInfo bufferInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17703:bufferInfo.size = 65536;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17704:bufferInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_VERTEX_BUFFER_BIT | VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17705:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17706:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17707:allocInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17708:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17709:VkBuffer buffer;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17710:VmaAllocation allocation;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17711:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufferInfo, &allocInfo, &buffer, &allocation, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17712:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17713:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17714:Don't forget to destroy your buffer and allocation objects when no longer needed:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17715:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17716:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17717:vmaDestroyBuffer(allocator, buffer, allocation);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17718:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17719:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17720:If you need to map the buffer, you must set flag
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17721:#VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT or #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17722:in VmaAllocationCreateInfo::flags.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17723:There are many additional parameters that can control the choice of memory type to be used for the allocation
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17724:and other features.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17725:For more information, see documentation chapters: @ref choosing_memory_type, @ref memory_mapping.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17726:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17727:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17728:\page choosing_memory_type Choosing memory type
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17729:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17730:Physical devices in Vulkan support various combinations of memory heaps and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17731:types. Help with choosing correct and optimal memory type for your specific
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17732:resource is one of the key features of this library. You can use it by filling
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17733:appropriate members of VmaAllocationCreateInfo structure, as described below.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17734:You can also combine multiple methods.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17735:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17736:-# If you just want to find memory type index that meets your requirements, you
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17737:   can use function: vmaFindMemoryTypeIndexForBufferInfo(),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17738:   vmaFindMemoryTypeIndexForImageInfo(), vmaFindMemoryTypeIndex().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17739:-# If you want to allocate a region of device memory without association with any
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17740:   specific image or buffer, you can use function vmaAllocateMemory(). Usage of
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17741:   this function is not recommended and usually not needed.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17742:   vmaAllocateMemoryPages() function is also provided for creating multiple allocations at once,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17743:   which may be useful for sparse binding.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17744:-# If you already have a buffer or an image created, you want to allocate memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17745:   for it and then you will bind it yourself, you can use function
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17746:   vmaAllocateMemoryForBuffer(), vmaAllocateMemoryForImage().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17747:   For binding you should use functions: vmaBindBufferMemory(), vmaBindImageMemory()
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17748:   or their extended versions: vmaBindBufferMemory2(), vmaBindImageMemory2().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17749:-# If you want to create a buffer or an image, allocate memory for it, and bind
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17750:   them together, all in one call, you can use function vmaCreateBuffer(),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17751:   vmaCreateImage().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17752:   <b>This is the easiest and recommended way to use this library!</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17753:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17754:When using 3. or 4., the library internally queries Vulkan for memory types
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17755:supported for that buffer or image (function `vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements()`)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17756:and uses only one of these types.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17757:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17758:If no memory type can be found that meets all the requirements, these functions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17759:return `VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17760:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17761:You can leave VmaAllocationCreateInfo structure completely filled with zeros.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17762:It means no requirements are specified for memory type.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17763:It is valid, although not very useful.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17764:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17765:\section choosing_memory_type_usage Usage
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17766:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17767:The easiest way to specify memory requirements is to fill member
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17768:VmaAllocationCreateInfo::usage using one of the values of enum #VmaMemoryUsage.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17769:It defines high level, common usage types.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17770:Since version 3 of the library, it is recommended to use #VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO to let it select best memory type for your resource automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17771:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17772:For example, if you want to create a uniform buffer that will be filled using
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17773:transfer only once or infrequently and then used for rendering every frame as a uniform buffer, you can
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17774:do it using following code. The buffer will most likely end up in a memory type with
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17775:`VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT` to be fast to access by the GPU device.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17776:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17777:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17778:VkBufferCreateInfo bufferInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17779:bufferInfo.size = 65536;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17780:bufferInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_UNIFORM_BUFFER_BIT | VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17781:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17782:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17783:allocInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17784:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17785:VkBuffer buffer;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17786:VmaAllocation allocation;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17787:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufferInfo, &allocInfo, &buffer, &allocation, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17788:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17789:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17790:If you have a preference for putting the resource in GPU (device) memory or CPU (host) memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17791:on systems with discrete graphics card that have the memories separate, you can use
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17792:#VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO_PREFER_DEVICE or #VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO_PREFER_HOST.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17793:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17794:When using `VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO*` while you want to map the allocated memory,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17795:you also need to specify one of the host access flags:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17796:#VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT or #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17797:This will help the library decide about preferred memory type to ensure it has `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17798:so you can map it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17799:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17800:For example, a staging buffer that will be filled via mapped pointer and then
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17801:used as a source of transfer to the buffer described previously can be created like this.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17802:It will likely end up in a memory type that is `HOST_VISIBLE` and `HOST_COHERENT`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17803:but not `HOST_CACHED` (meaning uncached, write-combined) and not `DEVICE_LOCAL` (meaning system RAM).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17804:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17805:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17806:VkBufferCreateInfo stagingBufferInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17807:stagingBufferInfo.size = 65536;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17808:stagingBufferInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17809:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17810:VmaAllocationCreateInfo stagingAllocInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17811:stagingAllocInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17812:stagingAllocInfo.flags = VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17813:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17814:VkBuffer stagingBuffer;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17815:VmaAllocation stagingAllocation;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17816:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &stagingBufferInfo, &stagingAllocInfo, &stagingBuffer, &stagingAllocation, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17817:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17818:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17819:For more examples of creating different kinds of resources, see chapter \ref usage_patterns.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17820:See also: @ref memory_mapping.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17821:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17822:Usage values `VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO*` are legal to use only when the library knows
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17823:about the resource being created by having `VkBufferCreateInfo` / `VkImageCreateInfo` passed,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17824:so they work with functions like: vmaCreateBuffer(), vmaCreateImage(), vmaFindMemoryTypeIndexForBufferInfo() etc.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17825:If you allocate raw memory using function vmaAllocateMemory(), you have to use other means of selecting
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17826:memory type, as described below.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17827:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17828:\note
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17829:Old usage values (`VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_GPU_ONLY`, `VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_ONLY`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17830:`VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_TO_GPU`, `VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_GPU_TO_CPU`, `VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_COPY`)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17831:are still available and work same way as in previous versions of the library
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17832:for backward compatibility, but they are deprecated.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17833:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17834:\section choosing_memory_type_required_preferred_flags Required and preferred flags
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17835:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17836:You can specify more detailed requirements by filling members
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17837:VmaAllocationCreateInfo::requiredFlags and VmaAllocationCreateInfo::preferredFlags
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17838:with a combination of bits from enum `VkMemoryPropertyFlags`. For example,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17839:if you want to create a buffer that will be persistently mapped on host (so it
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17840:must be `HOST_VISIBLE`) and preferably will also be `HOST_COHERENT` and `HOST_CACHED`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17841:use following code:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17842:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17843:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17844:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17845:allocInfo.requiredFlags = VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17846:allocInfo.preferredFlags = VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT | VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_CACHED_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17847:allocInfo.flags = VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT | VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17848:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17849:VkBuffer buffer;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17850:VmaAllocation allocation;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17851:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufferInfo, &allocInfo, &buffer, &allocation, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17852:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17853:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17854:A memory type is chosen that has all the required flags and as many preferred
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17855:flags set as possible.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17856:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17857:Value passed in VmaAllocationCreateInfo::usage is internally converted to a set of required and preferred flags,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17858:plus some extra "magic" (heuristics).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17859:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17860:\section choosing_memory_type_explicit_memory_types Explicit memory types
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17861:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17862:If you inspected memory types available on the physical device and <b>you have
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17863:a preference for memory types that you want to use</b>, you can fill member
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17864:VmaAllocationCreateInfo::memoryTypeBits. It is a bit mask, where each bit set
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17865:means that a memory type with that index is allowed to be used for the
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17866:allocation. Special value 0, just like `UINT32_MAX`, means there are no
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17867:restrictions to memory type index.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17868:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17869:Please note that this member is NOT just a memory type index.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17870:Still you can use it to choose just one, specific memory type.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17871:For example, if you already determined that your buffer should be created in
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17872:memory type 2, use following code:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17873:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17874:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17875:uint32_t memoryTypeIndex = 2;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17876:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17877:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17878:allocInfo.memoryTypeBits = 1U << memoryTypeIndex;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17879:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17880:VkBuffer buffer;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17881:VmaAllocation allocation;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17882:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufferInfo, &allocInfo, &buffer, &allocation, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17883:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17884:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17885:You can also use this parameter to <b>exclude some memory types</b>.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17886:If you inspect memory heaps and types available on the current physical device and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17887:you determine that for some reason you don't want to use a specific memory type for the allocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17888:you can enable automatic memory type selection but exclude certain memory type or types
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17889:by setting all bits of `memoryTypeBits` to 1 except the ones you choose.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17890:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17891:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17892:// ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17893:uint32_t excludedMemoryTypeIndex = 2;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17894:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17895:allocInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17896:allocInfo.memoryTypeBits = ~(1U << excludedMemoryTypeIndex);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17897:// ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17898:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17899:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17900:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17901:\section choosing_memory_type_custom_memory_pools Custom memory pools
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17902:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17903:If you allocate from custom memory pool, all the ways of specifying memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17904:requirements described above are not applicable and the aforementioned members
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17905:of VmaAllocationCreateInfo structure are ignored. Memory type is selected
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17906:explicitly when creating the pool and then used to make all the allocations from
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17907:that pool. For further details, see \ref custom_memory_pools.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17908:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17909:\section choosing_memory_type_dedicated_allocations Dedicated allocations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17910:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17911:Memory for allocations is reserved out of larger block of `VkDeviceMemory`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17912:allocated from Vulkan internally. That is the main feature of this whole library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17913:You can still request a separate memory block to be created for an allocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17914:just like you would do in a trivial solution without using any allocator.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17915:In that case, a buffer or image is always bound to that memory at offset 0.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17916:This is called a "dedicated allocation".
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17917:You can explicitly request it by using flag #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17918:The library can also internally decide to use dedicated allocation in some cases, e.g.:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17919:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17920:- When the size of the allocation is large.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17921:- When [VK_KHR_dedicated_allocation](@ref vk_khr_dedicated_allocation) extension is enabled
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17922:  and it reports that dedicated allocation is required or recommended for the resource.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17923:- When allocation of next big memory block fails due to not enough device memory,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17924:  but allocation with the exact requested size succeeds.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17925:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17926:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17927:\page memory_mapping Memory mapping
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17928:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17929:To "map memory" in Vulkan means to obtain a CPU pointer to `VkDeviceMemory`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17930:to be able to read from it or write to it in CPU code.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17931:Mapping is possible only of memory allocated from a memory type that has
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17932:`VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT` flag.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17933:Functions `vkMapMemory()`, `vkUnmapMemory()` are designed for this purpose.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17934:You can use them directly with memory allocated by this library,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17935:but it is not recommended because of following issue:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17936:Mapping the same `VkDeviceMemory` block multiple times is illegal - only one mapping at a time is allowed.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17937:This includes mapping disjoint regions. Mapping is not reference-counted internally by Vulkan.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17938:It is also not thread-safe.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17939:Because of this, Vulkan Memory Allocator provides following facilities:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17940:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17941:\note If you want to be able to map an allocation, you need to specify one of the flags
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17942:#VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT or #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17943:in VmaAllocationCreateInfo::flags. These flags are required for an allocation to be mappable
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17944:when using #VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO or other `VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO*` enum values.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17945:For other usage values they are ignored and every such allocation made in `HOST_VISIBLE` memory type is mappable,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17946:but these flags can still be used for consistency.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17947:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17948:\section memory_mapping_copy_functions Copy functions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17949:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17950:The easiest way to copy data from a host pointer to an allocation is to use convenience function vmaCopyMemoryToAllocation().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17951:It automatically maps the Vulkan memory temporarily (if not already mapped), performs `memcpy`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17952:and calls `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges` (if required - if memory type is not `HOST_COHERENT`).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17953:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17954:It is also the safest one, because using `memcpy` avoids a risk of accidentally introducing memory reads
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17955:(e.g. by doing `pMappedVectors[i] += v`), which may be very slow on memory types that are not `HOST_CACHED`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17956:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17957:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17958:struct ConstantBuffer
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17959:{
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17960:    ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17961:};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17962:ConstantBuffer constantBufferData = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17963:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17964:VkBufferCreateInfo bufCreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17965:bufCreateInfo.size = sizeof(ConstantBuffer);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17966:bufCreateInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17967:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17968:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17969:allocCreateInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17970:allocCreateInfo.flags = VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17971:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17972:VkBuffer buf;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17973:VmaAllocation alloc;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17974:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufCreateInfo, &allocCreateInfo, &buf, &alloc, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17975:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17976:vmaCopyMemoryToAllocation(allocator, &constantBufferData, alloc, 0, sizeof(ConstantBuffer));
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17977:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17978:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17979:Copy in the other direction - from an allocation to a host pointer can be performed the same way using function vmaCopyAllocationToMemory().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17980:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17981:\section memory_mapping_mapping_functions Mapping functions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17982:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17983:The library provides following functions for mapping of a specific allocation: vmaMapMemory(), vmaUnmapMemory().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17984:They are safer and more convenient to use than standard Vulkan functions.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17985:You can map an allocation multiple times simultaneously - mapping is reference-counted internally.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17986:You can also map different allocations simultaneously regardless of whether they use the same `VkDeviceMemory` block.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17987:The way it is implemented is that the library always maps entire memory block, not just region of the allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17988:For further details, see description of vmaMapMemory() function.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17989:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17990:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17991:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17992:// Having these objects initialized:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17993:struct ConstantBuffer
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17994:{
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17995:    ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17996:};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17997:ConstantBuffer constantBufferData = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17998:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:17999:VmaAllocator allocator = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18000:VkBuffer constantBuffer = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18001:VmaAllocation constantBufferAllocation = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18002:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18003:// You can map and fill your buffer using following code:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18004:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18005:void* mappedData;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18006:vmaMapMemory(allocator, constantBufferAllocation, &mappedData);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18007:memcpy(mappedData, &constantBufferData, sizeof(constantBufferData));
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18008:vmaUnmapMemory(allocator, constantBufferAllocation);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18009:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18010:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18011:When mapping, you may see a warning from Vulkan validation layer similar to this one:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18012:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18013:<i>Mapping an image with layout VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL can result in undefined behavior if this memory is used by the device. Only GENERAL or PREINITIALIZED should be used.</i>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18014:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18015:It happens because the library maps entire `VkDeviceMemory` block, where different
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18016:types of images and buffers may end up together, especially on GPUs with unified memory like Intel.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18017:You can safely ignore it if you are sure you access only memory of the intended
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18018:object that you wanted to map.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18019:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18020:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18021:\section memory_mapping_persistently_mapped_memory Persistently mapped memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18022:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18023:Keeping your memory persistently mapped is generally OK in Vulkan.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18024:You don't need to unmap it before using its data on the GPU.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18025:The library provides a special feature designed for that:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18026:Allocations made with #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT flag set in
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18027:VmaAllocationCreateInfo::flags stay mapped all the time,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18028:so you can just access CPU pointer to it any time
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18029:without a need to call any "map" or "unmap" function.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18030:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18031:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18032:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18033:VkBufferCreateInfo bufCreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18034:bufCreateInfo.size = sizeof(ConstantBuffer);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18035:bufCreateInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18036:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18037:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18038:allocCreateInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18039:allocCreateInfo.flags = VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT |
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18040:    VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18041:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18042:VkBuffer buf;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18043:VmaAllocation alloc;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18044:VmaAllocationInfo allocInfo;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18045:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufCreateInfo, &allocCreateInfo, &buf, &alloc, &allocInfo);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18046:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18047:// Buffer is already mapped. You can access its memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18048:memcpy(allocInfo.pMappedData, &constantBufferData, sizeof(constantBufferData));
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18049:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18050:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18051:\note #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT by itself doesn't guarantee that the allocation will end up
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18052:in a mappable memory type.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18053:For this, you need to also specify #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT or
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18054:#VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18055:#VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT only guarantees that if the memory is `HOST_VISIBLE`, the allocation will be mapped on creation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18056:For an example of how to make use of this fact, see section \ref usage_patterns_advanced_data_uploading.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18057:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18058:\section memory_mapping_cache_control Cache flush and invalidate
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18059:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18060:Memory in Vulkan doesn't need to be unmapped before using it on GPU,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18061:but unless a memory types has `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT` flag set,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18062:you need to manually **invalidate** cache before reading of mapped pointer
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18063:and **flush** cache after writing to mapped pointer.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18064:Map/unmap operations don't do that automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18065:Vulkan provides following functions for this purpose `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges()`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18066:`vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges()`, but this library provides more convenient
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18067:functions that refer to given allocation object: vmaFlushAllocation(),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18068:vmaInvalidateAllocation(),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18069:or multiple objects at once: vmaFlushAllocations(), vmaInvalidateAllocations().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18070:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18071:Regions of memory specified for flush/invalidate must be aligned to
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18072:`VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::nonCoherentAtomSize`. This is automatically ensured by the library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18073:In any memory type that is `HOST_VISIBLE` but not `HOST_COHERENT`, all allocations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18074:within blocks are aligned to this value, so their offsets are always multiply of
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18075:`nonCoherentAtomSize` and two different allocations never share same "line" of this size.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18076:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18077:Also, Windows drivers from all 3 PC GPU vendors (AMD, Intel, NVIDIA)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18078:currently provide `HOST_COHERENT` flag on all memory types that are
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18079:`HOST_VISIBLE`, so on PC you may not need to bother.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18080:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18081:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18082:\page staying_within_budget Staying within budget
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18083:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18084:When developing a graphics-intensive game or program, it is important to avoid allocating
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18085:more GPU memory than it is physically available. When the memory is over-committed,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18086:various bad things can happen, depending on the specific GPU, graphics driver, and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18087:operating system:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18088:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18089:- It may just work without any problems.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18090:- The application may slow down because some memory blocks are moved to system RAM
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18091:  and the GPU has to access them through PCI Express bus.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18092:- A new allocation may take very long time to complete, even few seconds, and possibly
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18093:  freeze entire system.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18094:- The new allocation may fail with `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18095:- It may even result in GPU crash (TDR), observed as `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18096:  returned somewhere later.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18097:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18098:\section staying_within_budget_querying_for_budget Querying for budget
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18099:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18100:To query for current memory usage and available budget, use function vmaGetHeapBudgets().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18101:Returned structure #VmaBudget contains quantities expressed in bytes, per Vulkan memory heap.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18102:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18103:Please note that this function returns different information and works faster than
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18104:vmaCalculateStatistics(). vmaGetHeapBudgets() can be called every frame or even before every
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18105:allocation, while vmaCalculateStatistics() is intended to be used rarely,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18106:only to obtain statistical information, e.g. for debugging purposes.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18107:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18108:It is recommended to use <b>VK_EXT_memory_budget</b> device extension to obtain information
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18109:about the budget from Vulkan device. VMA is able to use this extension automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18110:When not enabled, the allocator behaves same way, but then it estimates current usage
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18111:and available budget based on its internal information and Vulkan memory heap sizes,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18112:which may be less precise. In order to use this extension:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18113:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18114:1. Make sure extensions VK_EXT_memory_budget and VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18115:   required by it are available and enable them. Please note that the first is a device
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18116:   extension and the second is instance extension!
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18117:2. Use flag #VMA_ALLOCATOR_CREATE_EXT_MEMORY_BUDGET_BIT when creating #VmaAllocator object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18118:3. Make sure to call vmaSetCurrentFrameIndex() every frame. Budget is queried from
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18119:   Vulkan inside of it to avoid overhead of querying it with every allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18120:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18121:\section staying_within_budget_controlling_memory_usage Controlling memory usage
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18122:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18123:There are many ways in which you can try to stay within the budget.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18124:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18125:First, when making new allocation requires allocating a new memory block, the library
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18126:tries not to exceed the budget automatically. If a block with default recommended size
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18127:(e.g. 256 MB) would go over budget, a smaller block is allocated, possibly even
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18128:dedicated memory for just this resource.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18129:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18130:If the size of the requested resource plus current memory usage is more than the
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18131:budget, by default the library still tries to create it, leaving it to the Vulkan
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18132:implementation whether the allocation succeeds or fails. You can change this behavior
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18133:by using #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_WITHIN_BUDGET_BIT flag. With it, the allocation is
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18134:not made if it would exceed the budget or if the budget is already exceeded.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18135:VMA then tries to make the allocation from the next eligible Vulkan memory type.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18136:If all of them fail, the call then fails with `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18137:Example usage pattern may be to pass the #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_WITHIN_BUDGET_BIT flag
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18138:when creating resources that are not essential for the application (e.g. the texture
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18139:of a specific object) and not to pass it when creating critically important resources
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18140:(e.g. render targets).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18141:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18142:On AMD graphics cards there is a custom vendor extension available: <b>VK_AMD_memory_overallocation_behavior</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18143:that allows to control the behavior of the Vulkan implementation in out-of-memory cases -
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18144:whether it should fail with an error code or still allow the allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18145:Usage of this extension involves only passing extra structure on Vulkan device creation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18146:so it is out of scope of this library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18147:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18148:Finally, you can also use #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_NEVER_ALLOCATE_BIT flag to make sure
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18149:a new allocation is created only when it fits inside one of the existing memory blocks.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18150:If it would require to allocate a new block, if fails instead with `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18151:This also ensures that the function call is very fast because it never goes to Vulkan
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18152:to obtain a new block.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18153:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18154:\note Creating \ref custom_memory_pools with VmaPoolCreateInfo::minBlockCount
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18155:set to more than 0 will currently try to allocate memory blocks without checking whether they
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18156:fit within budget.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18157:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18158:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18159:\page resource_aliasing Resource aliasing (overlap)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18160:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18161:New explicit graphics APIs (Vulkan and Direct3D 12), thanks to manual memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18162:management, give an opportunity to alias (overlap) multiple resources in the
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18163:same region of memory - a feature not available in the old APIs (Direct3D 11, OpenGL).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18164:It can be useful to save video memory, but it must be used with caution.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18165:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18166:For example, if you know the flow of your whole render frame in advance, you
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18167:are going to use some intermediate textures or buffers only during a small range of render passes,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18168:and you know these ranges don't overlap in time, you can bind these resources to
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18169:the same place in memory, even if they have completely different parameters (width, height, format etc.).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18170:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18171:![Resource aliasing (overlap)](../gfx/Aliasing.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18172:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18173:Such scenario is possible using VMA, but you need to create your images manually.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18174:Then you need to calculate parameters of an allocation to be made using formula:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18175:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18176:- allocation size = max(size of each image)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18177:- allocation alignment = max(alignment of each image)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18178:- allocation memoryTypeBits = bitwise AND(memoryTypeBits of each image)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18179:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18180:Following example shows two different images bound to the same place in memory,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18181:allocated to fit largest of them.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18182:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18183:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18184:// A 512x512 texture to be sampled.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18185:VkImageCreateInfo img1CreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18186:img1CreateInfo.imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18187:img1CreateInfo.extent.width = 512;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18188:img1CreateInfo.extent.height = 512;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18189:img1CreateInfo.extent.depth = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18190:img1CreateInfo.mipLevels = 10;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18191:img1CreateInfo.arrayLayers = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18192:img1CreateInfo.format = VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18193:img1CreateInfo.tiling = VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL;
