src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18194:img1CreateInfo.initialLayout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18195:img1CreateInfo.usage = VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_SAMPLED_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18196:img1CreateInfo.samples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18197:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18198:// A full screen texture to be used as color attachment.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18199:VkImageCreateInfo img2CreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18200:img2CreateInfo.imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18201:img2CreateInfo.extent.width = 1920;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18202:img2CreateInfo.extent.height = 1080;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18203:img2CreateInfo.extent.depth = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18204:img2CreateInfo.mipLevels = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18205:img2CreateInfo.arrayLayers = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18206:img2CreateInfo.format = VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18207:img2CreateInfo.tiling = VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18208:img2CreateInfo.initialLayout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18209:img2CreateInfo.usage = VK_IMAGE_USAGE_SAMPLED_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18210:img2CreateInfo.samples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18211:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18212:VkImage img1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18213:res = vkCreateImage(device, &img1CreateInfo, nullptr, &img1);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18214:VkImage img2;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18215:res = vkCreateImage(device, &img2CreateInfo, nullptr, &img2);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18216:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18217:VkMemoryRequirements img1MemReq;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18218:vkGetImageMemoryRequirements(device, img1, &img1MemReq);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18219:VkMemoryRequirements img2MemReq;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18220:vkGetImageMemoryRequirements(device, img2, &img2MemReq);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18221:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18222:VkMemoryRequirements finalMemReq = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18223:finalMemReq.size = std::max(img1MemReq.size, img2MemReq.size);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18224:finalMemReq.alignment = std::max(img1MemReq.alignment, img2MemReq.alignment);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18225:finalMemReq.memoryTypeBits = img1MemReq.memoryTypeBits & img2MemReq.memoryTypeBits;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18226:// Validate if(finalMemReq.memoryTypeBits != 0)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18227:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18228:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18229:allocCreateInfo.preferredFlags = VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18230:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18231:VmaAllocation alloc;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18232:res = vmaAllocateMemory(allocator, &finalMemReq, &allocCreateInfo, &alloc, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18233:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18234:res = vmaBindImageMemory(allocator, alloc, img1);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18235:res = vmaBindImageMemory(allocator, alloc, img2);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18236:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18237:// You can use img1, img2 here, but not at the same time!
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18238:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18239:vmaFreeMemory(allocator, alloc);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18240:vkDestroyImage(allocator, img2, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18241:vkDestroyImage(allocator, img1, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18242:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18243:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18244:VMA also provides convenience functions that create a buffer or image and bind it to memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18245:represented by an existing #VmaAllocation:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18246:vmaCreateAliasingBuffer(), vmaCreateAliasingBuffer2(),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18247:vmaCreateAliasingImage(), vmaCreateAliasingImage2().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18248:Versions with "2" offer additional parameter `allocationLocalOffset`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18249:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18250:Remember that using resources that alias in memory requires proper synchronization.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18251:You need to issue a memory barrier to make sure commands that use `img1` and `img2`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18252:don't overlap on GPU timeline.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18253:You also need to treat a resource after aliasing as uninitialized - containing garbage data.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18254:For example, if you use `img1` and then want to use `img2`, you need to issue
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18255:an image memory barrier for `img2` with `oldLayout` = `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18256:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18257:Additional considerations:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18258:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18259:- Vulkan also allows to interpret contents of memory between aliasing resources consistently in some cases.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18260:See chapter 11.8. "Memory Aliasing" of Vulkan specification or `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_ALIAS_BIT` flag.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18261:- You can create more complex layout where different images and buffers are bound
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18262:at different offsets inside one large allocation. For example, one can imagine
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18263:a big texture used in some render passes, aliasing with a set of many small buffers
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18264:used between in some further passes. To bind a resource at non-zero offset in an allocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18265:use vmaBindBufferMemory2() / vmaBindImageMemory2().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18266:- Before allocating memory for the resources you want to alias, check `memoryTypeBits`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18267:returned in memory requirements of each resource to make sure the bits overlap.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18268:Some GPUs may expose multiple memory types suitable e.g. only for buffers or
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18269:images with `COLOR_ATTACHMENT` usage, so the sets of memory types supported by your
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18270:resources may be disjoint. Aliasing them is not possible in that case.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18271:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18272:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18273:\page custom_memory_pools Custom memory pools
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18274:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18275:A memory pool contains a number of `VkDeviceMemory` blocks.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18276:The library automatically creates and manages default pool for each memory type available on the device.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18277:Default memory pool automatically grows in size.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18278:Size of allocated blocks is also variable and managed automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18279:You are using default pools whenever you leave VmaAllocationCreateInfo::pool = null.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18280:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18281:You can create custom pool and allocate memory out of it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18282:It can be useful if you want to:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18283:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18284:- Keep certain kind of allocations separate from others.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18285:- Enforce particular, fixed size of Vulkan memory blocks.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18286:- Limit maximum amount of Vulkan memory allocated for that pool.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18287:- Reserve minimum or fixed amount of Vulkan memory always preallocated for that pool.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18288:- Use extra parameters for a set of your allocations that are available in #VmaPoolCreateInfo but not in
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18289:  #VmaAllocationCreateInfo - e.g., custom minimum alignment, custom `pNext` chain.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18290:- Perform defragmentation on a specific subset of your allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18291:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18292:To use custom memory pools:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18293:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18294:-# Fill VmaPoolCreateInfo structure.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18295:-# Call vmaCreatePool() to obtain #VmaPool handle.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18296:-# When making an allocation, set VmaAllocationCreateInfo::pool to this handle.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18297:   You don't need to specify any other parameters of this structure, like `usage`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18298:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18299:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18300:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18301:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18302:// Find memoryTypeIndex for the pool.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18303:VkBufferCreateInfo sampleBufCreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18304:sampleBufCreateInfo.size = 0x10000; // Doesn't matter.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18305:sampleBufCreateInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_UNIFORM_BUFFER_BIT | VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18306:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18307:VmaAllocationCreateInfo sampleAllocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18308:sampleAllocCreateInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18309:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18310:uint32_t memTypeIndex;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18311:VkResult res = vmaFindMemoryTypeIndexForBufferInfo(allocator,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18312:    &sampleBufCreateInfo, &sampleAllocCreateInfo, &memTypeIndex);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18313:// Check res...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18314:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18315:// Create a pool that can have at most 2 blocks, 128 MiB each.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18316:VmaPoolCreateInfo poolCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18317:poolCreateInfo.memoryTypeIndex = memTypeIndex;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18318:poolCreateInfo.blockSize = 128ULL * 1024 * 1024;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18319:poolCreateInfo.maxBlockCount = 2;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18320:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18321:VmaPool pool;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18322:res = vmaCreatePool(allocator, &poolCreateInfo, &pool);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18323:// Check res...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18324:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18325:// Allocate a buffer out of it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18326:VkBufferCreateInfo bufCreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18327:bufCreateInfo.size = 1024;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18328:bufCreateInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_UNIFORM_BUFFER_BIT | VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18329:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18330:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18331:allocCreateInfo.pool = pool;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18332:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18333:VkBuffer buf;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18334:VmaAllocation alloc;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18335:res = vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufCreateInfo, &allocCreateInfo, &buf, &alloc, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18336:// Check res...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18337:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18338:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18339:You have to free all allocations made from this pool before destroying it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18340:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18341:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18342:vmaDestroyBuffer(allocator, buf, alloc);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18343:vmaDestroyPool(allocator, pool);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18344:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18345:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18346:New versions of this library support creating dedicated allocations in custom pools.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18347:It is supported only when VmaPoolCreateInfo::blockSize = 0.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18348:To use this feature, set VmaAllocationCreateInfo::pool to the pointer to your custom pool and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18349:VmaAllocationCreateInfo::flags to #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18350:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18351:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18352:\section custom_memory_pools_MemTypeIndex Choosing memory type index
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18353:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18354:When creating a pool, you must explicitly specify memory type index.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18355:To find the one suitable for your buffers or images, you can use helper functions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18356:vmaFindMemoryTypeIndexForBufferInfo(), vmaFindMemoryTypeIndexForImageInfo().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18357:You need to provide structures with example parameters of buffers or images
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18358:that you are going to create in that pool.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18359:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18360:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18361:VkBufferCreateInfo exampleBufCreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18362:exampleBufCreateInfo.size = 1024; // Doesn't matter
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18363:exampleBufCreateInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_UNIFORM_BUFFER_BIT | VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18364:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18365:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18366:allocCreateInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18367:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18368:uint32_t memTypeIndex;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18369:vmaFindMemoryTypeIndexForBufferInfo(allocator, &exampleBufCreateInfo, &allocCreateInfo, &memTypeIndex);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18370:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18371:VmaPoolCreateInfo poolCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18372:poolCreateInfo.memoryTypeIndex = memTypeIndex;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18373:// ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18374:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18375:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18376:When creating buffers/images allocated in that pool, provide following parameters:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18377:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18378:- `VkBufferCreateInfo`: Prefer to pass same parameters as above.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18379:  Otherwise you risk creating resources in a memory type that is not suitable for them, which may result in undefined behavior.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18380:  Using different `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_` flags may work, but you shouldn't create images in a pool intended for buffers
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18381:  or the other way around.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18382:- VmaAllocationCreateInfo: You don't need to pass same parameters. Fill only `pool` member.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18383:  Other members are ignored anyway.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18384:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18385:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18386:\section custom_memory_pools_when_not_use When not to use custom pools
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18387:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18388:Custom pools are commonly overused by VMA users.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18389:While it may feel natural to keep some logical groups of resources separate in memory,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18390:in most cases it does more harm than good.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18391:Using custom pool shouldn't be your first choice.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18392:Instead, please make all allocations from default pools first and only use custom pools
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18393:if you can prove and measure that it is beneficial in some way,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18394:e.g. it results in lower memory usage, better performance, etc.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18395:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18396:Using custom pools has disadvantages:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18397:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18398:- Each pool has its own collection of `VkDeviceMemory` blocks.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18399:  Some of them may be partially or even completely empty.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18400:  Spreading allocations across multiple pools increases the amount of wasted (allocated but unbound) memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18401:- You must manually choose specific memory type to be used by a custom pool (set as VmaPoolCreateInfo::memoryTypeIndex).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18402:  When using default pools, best memory type for each of your allocations can be selected automatically
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18403:  using a carefully design algorithm that works across all kinds of GPUs.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18404:- If an allocation from a custom pool at specific memory type fails, entire allocation operation returns failure.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18405:  When using default pools, VMA tries another compatible memory type.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18406:- If you set VmaPoolCreateInfo::blockSize != 0, each memory block has the same size,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18407:  while default pools start from small blocks and only allocate next blocks larger and larger
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18408:  up to the preferred block size.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18409:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18410:Many of the common concerns can be addressed in a different way than using custom pools:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18411:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18412:- If you want to keep your allocations of certain size (small versus large) or certain lifetime (transient versus long lived)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18413:  separate, you likely don't need to.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18414:  VMA uses a high quality allocation algorithm that manages memory well in various cases.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18415:  Please measure and check if using custom pools provides a benefit.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18416:- If you want to keep your images and buffers separate, you don't need to.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18417:  VMA respects `bufferImageGranularity` limit automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18418:- If you want to keep your mapped and not mapped allocations separate, you don't need to.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18419:  VMA respects `nonCoherentAtomSize` limit automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18420:  It also maps only those `VkDeviceMemory` blocks that need to map any allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18421:  It even tries to keep mappable and non-mappable allocations in separate blocks to minimize the amount of mapped memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18422:- If you want to choose a custom size for the default memory block, you can set it globally instead
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18423:  using VmaAllocatorCreateInfo::preferredLargeHeapBlockSize.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18424:- If you want to select specific memory type for your allocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18425:  you can set VmaAllocationCreateInfo::memoryTypeBits to `(1U << myMemoryTypeIndex)` instead.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18426:- If you need to create a buffer with certain minimum alignment, you can still do it
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18427:  using default pools by specifying VmaAllocationCreateInfo::minAlignment.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18428:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18429:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18430:\section linear_algorithm Linear allocation algorithm
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18431:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18432:Each Vulkan memory block managed by this library has accompanying metadata that
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18433:keeps track of used and unused regions. By default, the metadata structure and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18434:algorithm tries to find best place for new allocations among free regions to
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18435:optimize memory usage. This way you can allocate and free objects in any order.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18436:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18437:![Default allocation algorithm](../gfx/Linear_allocator_1_algo_default.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18438:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18439:Sometimes there is a need to use simpler, linear allocation algorithm. You can
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18440:create custom pool that uses such algorithm by adding flag
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18441:#VMA_POOL_CREATE_LINEAR_ALGORITHM_BIT to VmaPoolCreateInfo::flags while creating
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18442:#VmaPool object. Then an alternative metadata management is used. It always
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18443:creates new allocations after last one and doesn't reuse free regions after
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18444:allocations freed in the middle. It results in better allocation performance and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18445:less memory consumed by metadata.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18446:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18447:![Linear allocation algorithm](../gfx/Linear_allocator_2_algo_linear.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18448:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18449:With this one flag, you can create a custom pool that can be used in many ways:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18450:free-at-once, stack, double stack, and ring buffer. See below for details.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18451:You don't need to specify explicitly which of these options you are going to use - it is detected automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18452:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18453:\subsection linear_algorithm_free_at_once Free-at-once
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18454:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18455:In a pool that uses linear algorithm, you still need to free all the allocations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18456:individually, e.g. by using vmaFreeMemory() or vmaDestroyBuffer(). You can free
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18457:them in any order. New allocations are always made after last one - free space
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18458:in the middle is not reused. However, when you release all the allocation and
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18459:the pool becomes empty, allocation starts from the beginning again. This way you
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18460:can use linear algorithm to speed up creation of allocations that you are going
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18461:to release all at once.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18462:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18463:![Free-at-once](../gfx/Linear_allocator_3_free_at_once.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18464:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18465:This mode is also available for pools created with VmaPoolCreateInfo::maxBlockCount
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18466:value that allows multiple memory blocks.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18467:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18468:\subsection linear_algorithm_stack Stack
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18469:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18470:When you free an allocation that was created last, its space can be reused.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18471:Thanks to this, if you always release allocations in the order opposite to their
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18472:creation (LIFO - Last In First Out), you can achieve behavior of a stack.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18473:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18474:![Stack](../gfx/Linear_allocator_4_stack.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18475:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18476:This mode is also available for pools created with VmaPoolCreateInfo::maxBlockCount
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18477:value that allows multiple memory blocks.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18478:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18479:\subsection linear_algorithm_double_stack Double stack
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18480:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18481:The space reserved by a custom pool with linear algorithm may be used by two
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18482:stacks:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18483:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18484:- First, default one, growing up from offset 0.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18485:- Second, "upper" one, growing down from the end towards lower offsets.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18486:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18487:To make allocation from the upper stack, add flag #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_UPPER_ADDRESS_BIT
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18488:to VmaAllocationCreateInfo::flags.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18489:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18490:![Double stack](../gfx/Linear_allocator_7_double_stack.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18491:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18492:Double stack is available only in pools with one memory block -
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18493:VmaPoolCreateInfo::maxBlockCount must be 1. Otherwise behavior is undefined.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18494:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18495:When the two stacks' ends meet so there is not enough space between them for a
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18496:new allocation, such allocation fails with usual
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18497:`VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` error.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18498:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18499:\subsection linear_algorithm_ring_buffer Ring buffer
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18500:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18501:When you free some allocations from the beginning and there is not enough free space
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18502:for a new one at the end of a pool, allocator's "cursor" wraps around to the
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18503:beginning and starts allocation there. Thanks to this, if you always release
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18504:allocations in the same order as you created them (FIFO - First In First Out),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18505:you can achieve behavior of a ring buffer / queue.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18506:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18507:![Ring buffer](../gfx/Linear_allocator_5_ring_buffer.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18508:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18509:Ring buffer is available only in pools with one memory block -
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18510:VmaPoolCreateInfo::maxBlockCount must be 1. Otherwise behavior is undefined.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18511:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18512:\note \ref defragmentation is not supported in custom pools created with #VMA_POOL_CREATE_LINEAR_ALGORITHM_BIT.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18513:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18514:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18515:\page defragmentation Defragmentation
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18516:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18517:Interleaved allocations and deallocations of many objects of varying size can
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18518:cause fragmentation over time, which can lead to a situation where the library is unable
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18519:to find a continuous range of free memory for a new allocation despite there is
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18520:enough free space, just scattered across many small free ranges between existing
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18521:allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18522:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18523:To mitigate this problem, you can use defragmentation feature.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18524:It doesn't happen automatically though and needs your cooperation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18525:because VMA is a low level library that only allocates memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18526:It cannot recreate buffers and images in a new place as it doesn't remember the contents of `VkBufferCreateInfo` / `VkImageCreateInfo` structures.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18527:It cannot copy their contents as it doesn't record any commands to a command buffer.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18528:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18529:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18530:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18531:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18532:VmaDefragmentationInfo defragInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18533:defragInfo.pool = myPool;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18534:defragInfo.flags = VMA_DEFRAGMENTATION_FLAG_ALGORITHM_FAST_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18535:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18536:VmaDefragmentationContext defragCtx;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18537:VkResult res = vmaBeginDefragmentation(allocator, &defragInfo, &defragCtx);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18538:// Check res...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18539:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18540:for(;;)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18541:{
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18542:    VmaDefragmentationPassMoveInfo pass;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18543:    res = vmaBeginDefragmentationPass(allocator, defragCtx, &pass);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18544:    if(res == VK_SUCCESS)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18545:        break;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18546:    else if(res != VK_INCOMPLETE)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18547:        // Handle error...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18548:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18549:    for(uint32_t i = 0; i < pass.moveCount; ++i)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18550:    {
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18551:        // Inspect pass.pMoves[i].srcAllocation, identify what buffer/image it represents.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18552:        VmaAllocationInfo allocInfo;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18553:        vmaGetAllocationInfo(allocator, pass.pMoves[i].srcAllocation, &allocInfo);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18554:        MyEngineResourceData* resData = (MyEngineResourceData*)allocInfo.pUserData;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18555:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18556:        // Recreate and bind this buffer/image at: pass.pMoves[i].dstMemory, pass.pMoves[i].dstOffset.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18557:        VkImageCreateInfo imgCreateInfo = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18558:        VkImage newImg;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18559:        res = vkCreateImage(device, &imgCreateInfo, nullptr, &newImg);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18560:        // Check res...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18561:        res = vmaBindImageMemory(allocator, pass.pMoves[i].dstTmpAllocation, newImg);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18562:        // Check res...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18563:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18564:        // Issue a vkCmdCopyBuffer/vkCmdCopyImage to copy its content to the new place.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18565:        vkCmdCopyImage(cmdBuf, resData->img, ..., newImg, ...);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18566:    }
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18567:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18568:    // Make sure the copy commands finished executing.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18569:    vkWaitForFences(...);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18570:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18571:    // Destroy old buffers/images bound with pass.pMoves[i].srcAllocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18572:    for(uint32_t i = 0; i < pass.moveCount; ++i)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18573:    {
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18574:        // ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18575:        vkDestroyImage(device, resData->img, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18576:    }
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18577:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18578:    // Update appropriate descriptors to point to the new places...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18579:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18580:    res = vmaEndDefragmentationPass(allocator, defragCtx, &pass);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18581:    if(res == VK_SUCCESS)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18582:        break;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18583:    else if(res != VK_INCOMPLETE)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18584:        // Handle error...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18585:}
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18586:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18587:vmaEndDefragmentation(allocator, defragCtx, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18588:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18589:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18590:Although functions like vmaCreateBuffer(), vmaCreateImage(), vmaDestroyBuffer(), vmaDestroyImage()
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18591:create/destroy an allocation and a buffer/image at once, these are just a shortcut for
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18592:creating the resource, allocating memory, and binding them together.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18593:Defragmentation works on memory allocations only. You must handle the rest manually.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18594:Defragmentation is an iterative process that should repreat "passes" as long as related functions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18595:return `VK_INCOMPLETE` not `VK_SUCCESS`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18596:In each pass:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18597:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18598:1. vmaBeginDefragmentationPass() function call:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18599:   - Calculates and returns the list of allocations to be moved in this pass.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18600:     Note this can be a time-consuming process.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18601:   - Reserves destination memory for them by creating temporary destination allocations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18602:     that you can query for their `VkDeviceMemory` + offset using vmaGetAllocationInfo().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18603:2. Inside the pass, **you should**:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18604:   - Inspect the returned list of allocations to be moved.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18605:   - Create new buffers/images and bind them at the returned destination temporary allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18606:   - Copy data from source to destination resources if necessary.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18607:   - Destroy the source buffers/images, but NOT their allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18608:3. vmaEndDefragmentationPass() function call:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18609:   - Frees the source memory reserved for the allocations that are moved.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18610:   - Modifies source #VmaAllocation objects that are moved to point to the destination reserved memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18611:   - Frees `VkDeviceMemory` blocks that became empty.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18612:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18613:Unlike in previous iterations of the defragmentation API, there is no list of "movable" allocations passed as a parameter.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18614:Defragmentation algorithm tries to move all suitable allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18615:You can, however, refuse to move some of them inside a defragmentation pass, by setting
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18616:`pass.pMoves[i].operation` to #VMA_DEFRAGMENTATION_MOVE_OPERATION_IGNORE.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18617:This is not recommended and may result in suboptimal packing of the allocations after defragmentation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18618:If you cannot ensure any allocation can be moved, it is better to keep movable allocations separate in a custom pool.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18619:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18620:Inside a pass, for each allocation that should be moved:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18621:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18622:- You should copy its data from the source to the destination place by calling e.g. `vkCmdCopyBuffer()`, `vkCmdCopyImage()`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18623:  - You need to make sure these commands finished executing before destroying the source buffers/images and before calling vmaEndDefragmentationPass().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18624:- If a resource doesn't contain any meaningful data, e.g. it is a transient color attachment image to be cleared,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18625:  filled, and used temporarily in each rendering frame, you can just recreate this image
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18626:  without copying its data.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18627:- If the resource is in `HOST_VISIBLE` and `HOST_CACHED` memory, you can copy its data on the CPU
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18628:  using `memcpy()`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18629:- If you cannot move the allocation, you can set `pass.pMoves[i].operation` to #VMA_DEFRAGMENTATION_MOVE_OPERATION_IGNORE.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18630:  This will cancel the move.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18631:  - vmaEndDefragmentationPass() will then free the destination memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18632:    not the source memory of the allocation, leaving it unchanged.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18633:- If you decide the allocation is unimportant and can be destroyed instead of moved (e.g. it wasn't used for long time),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18634:  you can set `pass.pMoves[i].operation` to #VMA_DEFRAGMENTATION_MOVE_OPERATION_DESTROY.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18635:  - vmaEndDefragmentationPass() will then free both source and destination memory, and will destroy the source #VmaAllocation object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18636:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18637:You can defragment a specific custom pool by setting VmaDefragmentationInfo::pool
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18638:(like in the example above) or all the default pools by setting this member to null.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18639:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18640:Defragmentation is always performed in each pool separately.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18641:Allocations are never moved between different Vulkan memory types.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18642:The size of the destination memory reserved for a moved allocation is the same as the original one.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18643:Alignment of an allocation as it was determined using `vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements()` etc. is also respected after defragmentation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18644:Buffers/images should be recreated with the same `VkBufferCreateInfo` / `VkImageCreateInfo` parameters as the original ones.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18645:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18646:You can perform the defragmentation incrementally to limit the number of allocations and bytes to be moved
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18647:in each pass, e.g. to call it in sync with render frames and not to experience too big hitches.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18648:See members: VmaDefragmentationInfo::maxBytesPerPass, VmaDefragmentationInfo::maxAllocationsPerPass.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18649:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18650:It is also safe to perform the defragmentation asynchronously to render frames and other Vulkan and VMA
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18651:usage, possibly from multiple threads, with the exception that allocations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18652:returned in VmaDefragmentationPassMoveInfo::pMoves shouldn't be destroyed until the defragmentation pass is ended.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18653:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18654:<b>Mapping</b> is preserved on allocations that are moved during defragmentation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18655:Whether through #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT or vmaMapMemory(), the allocations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18656:are mapped at their new place. Of course, pointer to the mapped data changes, so it needs to be queried
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18657:using VmaAllocationInfo::pMappedData.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18658:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18659:\note Defragmentation is not supported in custom pools created with #VMA_POOL_CREATE_LINEAR_ALGORITHM_BIT.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18660:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18661:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18662:\page statistics Statistics
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18663:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18664:This library contains several functions that return information about its internal state,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18665:especially the amount of memory allocated from Vulkan.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18666:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18667:\section statistics_numeric_statistics Numeric statistics
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18668:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18669:If you need to obtain basic statistics about memory usage per heap, together with current budget,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18670:you can call function vmaGetHeapBudgets() and inspect structure #VmaBudget.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18671:This is useful to keep track of memory usage and stay within budget
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18672:(see also \ref staying_within_budget).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18673:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18674:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18675:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18676:uint32_t heapIndex = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18677:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18678:VmaBudget budgets[VK_MAX_MEMORY_HEAPS];
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18679:vmaGetHeapBudgets(allocator, budgets);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18680:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18681:printf("My heap currently has %u allocations taking %llu B,\n",
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18682:    budgets[heapIndex].statistics.allocationCount,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18683:    budgets[heapIndex].statistics.allocationBytes);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18684:printf("allocated out of %u Vulkan device memory blocks taking %llu B,\n",
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18685:    budgets[heapIndex].statistics.blockCount,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18686:    budgets[heapIndex].statistics.blockBytes);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18687:printf("Vulkan reports total usage %llu B with budget %llu B.\n",
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18688:    budgets[heapIndex].usage,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18689:    budgets[heapIndex].budget);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18690:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18691:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18692:You can query for more detailed statistics per memory heap, type, and totals,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18693:including minimum and maximum allocation size and unused range size,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18694:by calling function vmaCalculateStatistics() and inspecting structure #VmaTotalStatistics.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18695:This function is slower though, as it has to traverse all the internal data structures,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18696:so it should be used only for debugging purposes.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18697:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18698:You can query for statistics of a custom pool using function vmaGetPoolStatistics()
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18699:or vmaCalculatePoolStatistics().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18700:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18701:You can query for information about a specific allocation using function vmaGetAllocationInfo().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18702:It fill structure #VmaAllocationInfo.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18703:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18704:\section statistics_json_dump JSON dump
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18705:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18706:You can dump internal state of the allocator to a string in JSON format using function vmaBuildStatsString().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18707:The result is guaranteed to be correct JSON.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18708:It uses ANSI encoding.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18709:Any strings provided by user (see [Allocation names](@ref allocation_names))
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18710:are copied as-is and properly escaped for JSON, so if they use UTF-8, ISO-8859-2 or any other encoding,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18711:this JSON string can be treated as using this encoding.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18712:It must be freed using function vmaFreeStatsString().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18713:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18714:The format of this JSON string is not part of official documentation of the library,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18715:but it will not change in backward-incompatible way without increasing library major version number
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18716:and appropriate mention in changelog.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18717:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18718:The JSON string contains all the data that can be obtained using vmaCalculateStatistics().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18719:It can also contain detailed map of allocated memory blocks and their regions -
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18720:free and occupied by allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18721:This allows e.g. to visualize the memory or assess fragmentation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18722:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18723:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18724:\page allocation_annotation Allocation names and user data
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18725:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18726:\section allocation_user_data Allocation user data
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18727:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18728:You can annotate allocations with your own information, e.g. for debugging purposes.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18729:To do that, fill VmaAllocationCreateInfo::pUserData field when creating
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18730:an allocation. It is an opaque `void*` pointer. You can use it e.g. as a pointer,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18731:some handle, index, key, ordinal number or any other value that would associate
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18732:the allocation with your custom metadata.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18733:It is useful to identify appropriate data structures in your engine given #VmaAllocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18734:e.g. when doing \ref defragmentation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18735:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18736:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18737:VkBufferCreateInfo bufCreateInfo = ...
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18738:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18739:MyBufferMetadata* pMetadata = CreateBufferMetadata();
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18740:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18741:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18742:allocCreateInfo.usage = VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18743:allocCreateInfo.pUserData = pMetadata;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18744:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18745:VkBuffer buffer;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18746:VmaAllocation allocation;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18747:vmaCreateBuffer(allocator, &bufCreateInfo, &allocCreateInfo, &buffer, &allocation, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18748:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18749:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18750:The pointer may be later retrieved as VmaAllocationInfo::pUserData:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18751:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18752:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18753:VmaAllocationInfo allocInfo;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18754:vmaGetAllocationInfo(allocator, allocation, &allocInfo);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18755:MyBufferMetadata* pMetadata = (MyBufferMetadata*)allocInfo.pUserData;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18756:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18757:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18758:It can also be changed using function vmaSetAllocationUserData().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18759:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18760:Values of (non-zero) allocations' `pUserData` are printed in JSON report created by
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18761:vmaBuildStatsString() in hexadecimal form.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18762:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18763:\section allocation_names Allocation names
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18764:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18765:An allocation can also carry a null-terminated string, giving a name to the allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18766:To set it, call vmaSetAllocationName().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18767:The library creates internal copy of the string, so the pointer you pass doesn't need
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18768:to be valid for whole lifetime of the allocation. You can free it after the call.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18769:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18770:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18771:std::string imageName = "Texture: ";
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18772:imageName += fileName;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18773:vmaSetAllocationName(allocator, allocation, imageName.c_str());
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18774:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18775:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18776:The string can be later retrieved by inspecting VmaAllocationInfo::pName.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18777:It is also printed in JSON report created by vmaBuildStatsString().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18778:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18779:\note Setting string name to VMA allocation doesn't automatically set it to the Vulkan buffer or image created with it.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18780:You must do it manually using an extension like VK_EXT_debug_utils, which is independent of this library.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18781:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18782:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18783:\page virtual_allocator Virtual allocator
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18784:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18785:As an extra feature, the core allocation algorithm of the library is exposed through a simple and convenient API of "virtual allocator".
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18786:It doesn't allocate any real GPU memory. It just keeps track of used and free regions of a "virtual block".
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18787:You can use it to allocate your own memory or other objects, even completely unrelated to Vulkan.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18788:A common use case is sub-allocation of pieces of one large GPU buffer.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18789:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18790:\section virtual_allocator_creating_virtual_block Creating virtual block
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18791:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18792:To use this functionality, there is no main "allocator" object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18793:You don't need to have #VmaAllocator object created.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18794:All you need to do is to create a separate #VmaVirtualBlock object for each block of memory you want to be managed by the allocator:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18795:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18796:-# Fill in #VmaVirtualBlockCreateInfo structure.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18797:-# Call vmaCreateVirtualBlock(). Get new #VmaVirtualBlock object.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18798:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18799:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18800:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18801:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18802:VmaVirtualBlockCreateInfo blockCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18803:blockCreateInfo.size = 1048576; // 1 MB
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18804:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18805:VmaVirtualBlock block;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18806:VkResult res = vmaCreateVirtualBlock(&blockCreateInfo, &block);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18807:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18808:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18809:\section virtual_allocator_making_virtual_allocations Making virtual allocations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18810:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18811:#VmaVirtualBlock object contains internal data structure that keeps track of free and occupied regions
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18812:using the same code as the main Vulkan memory allocator.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18813:Similarly to #VmaAllocation for standard GPU allocations, there is #VmaVirtualAllocation type
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18814:that represents an opaque handle to an allocation within the virtual block.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18815:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18816:In order to make such allocation:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18817:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18818:-# Fill in #VmaVirtualAllocationCreateInfo structure.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18819:-# Call vmaVirtualAllocate(). Get new #VmaVirtualAllocation object that represents the allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18820:   You can also receive `VkDeviceSize offset` that was assigned to the allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18821:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18822:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18823:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18824:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18825:VmaVirtualAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18826:allocCreateInfo.size = 4096; // 4 KB
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18827:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18828:VmaVirtualAllocation alloc;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18829:VkDeviceSize offset;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18830:res = vmaVirtualAllocate(block, &allocCreateInfo, &alloc, &offset);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18831:if(res == VK_SUCCESS)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18832:{
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18833:    // Use the 4 KB of your memory starting at offset.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18834:}
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18835:else
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18836:{
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18837:    // Allocation failed - no space for it could be found. Handle this error!
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18838:}
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18839:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18840:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18841:\section virtual_allocator_deallocation Deallocation
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18842:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18843:When no longer needed, an allocation can be freed by calling vmaVirtualFree().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18844:You can only pass to this function an allocation that was previously returned by vmaVirtualAllocate()
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18845:called for the same #VmaVirtualBlock.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18846:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18847:When whole block is no longer needed, the block object can be released by calling vmaDestroyVirtualBlock().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18848:All allocations must be freed before the block is destroyed, which is checked internally by an assert.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18849:However, if you don't want to call vmaVirtualFree() for each allocation, you can use vmaClearVirtualBlock() to free them all at once -
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18850:a feature not available in normal Vulkan memory allocator. Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18851:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18852:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18853:vmaVirtualFree(block, alloc);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18854:vmaDestroyVirtualBlock(block);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18855:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18856:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18857:\section virtual_allocator_allocation_parameters Allocation parameters
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18858:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18859:You can attach a custom pointer to each allocation by using vmaSetVirtualAllocationUserData().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18860:Its default value is null.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18861:It can be used to store any data that needs to be associated with that allocation - e.g. an index, a handle, or a pointer to some
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18862:larger data structure containing more information. Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18863:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18864:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18865:struct CustomAllocData
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18866:{
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18867:    std::string m_AllocName;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18868:};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18869:CustomAllocData* allocData = new CustomAllocData();
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18870:allocData->m_AllocName = "My allocation 1";
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18871:vmaSetVirtualAllocationUserData(block, alloc, allocData);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18872:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18873:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18874:The pointer can later be fetched, along with allocation offset and size, by passing the allocation handle to function
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18875:vmaGetVirtualAllocationInfo() and inspecting returned structure #VmaVirtualAllocationInfo.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18876:If you allocated a new object to be used as the custom pointer, don't forget to delete that object before freeing the allocation!
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18877:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18878:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18879:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18880:VmaVirtualAllocationInfo allocInfo;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18881:vmaGetVirtualAllocationInfo(block, alloc, &allocInfo);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18882:delete (CustomAllocData*)allocInfo.pUserData;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18883:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18884:vmaVirtualFree(block, alloc);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18885:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18886:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18887:\section virtual_allocator_alignment_and_units Alignment and units
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18888:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18889:It feels natural to express sizes and offsets in bytes.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18890:If an offset of an allocation needs to be aligned to a multiply of some number (e.g. 4 bytes), you can fill optional member
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18891:VmaVirtualAllocationCreateInfo::alignment to request it. Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18892:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18893:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18894:VmaVirtualAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18895:allocCreateInfo.size = 4096; // 4 KB
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18896:allocCreateInfo.alignment = 4; // Returned offset must be a multiply of 4 B
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18897:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18898:VmaVirtualAllocation alloc;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18899:res = vmaVirtualAllocate(block, &allocCreateInfo, &alloc, nullptr);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18900:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18901:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18902:Alignments of different allocations made from one block may vary.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18903:However, if all alignments and sizes are always multiply of some size e.g. 4 B or `sizeof(MyDataStruct)`,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18904:you can express all sizes, alignments, and offsets in multiples of that size instead of individual bytes.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18905:It might be more convenient, but you need to make sure to use this new unit consistently in all the places:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18906:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18907:- VmaVirtualBlockCreateInfo::size
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18908:- VmaVirtualAllocationCreateInfo::size and VmaVirtualAllocationCreateInfo::alignment
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18909:- Using offset returned by vmaVirtualAllocate() or in VmaVirtualAllocationInfo::offset
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18910:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18911:\section virtual_allocator_statistics Statistics
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18912:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18913:You can obtain statistics of a virtual block using vmaGetVirtualBlockStatistics()
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18914:(to get brief statistics that are fast to calculate)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18915:or vmaCalculateVirtualBlockStatistics() (to get more detailed statistics, slower to calculate).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18916:The functions fill structures #VmaStatistics, #VmaDetailedStatistics respectively - same as used by the normal Vulkan memory allocator.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18917:Example:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18918:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18919:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18920:VmaStatistics stats;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18921:vmaGetVirtualBlockStatistics(block, &stats);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18922:printf("My virtual block has %llu bytes used by %u virtual allocations\n",
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18923:    stats.allocationBytes, stats.allocationCount);
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18924:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18925:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18926:You can also request a full list of allocations and free regions as a string in JSON format by calling
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18927:vmaBuildVirtualBlockStatsString().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18928:Returned string must be later freed using vmaFreeVirtualBlockStatsString().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18929:The format of this string differs from the one returned by the main Vulkan allocator, but it is similar.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18930:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18931:\section virtual_allocator_additional_considerations Additional considerations
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18932:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18933:The "virtual allocator" functionality is implemented on a level of individual memory blocks.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18934:Keeping track of a whole collection of blocks, allocating new ones when out of free space,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18935:deleting empty ones, and deciding which one to try first for a new allocation must be implemented by the user.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18936:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18937:Alternative allocation algorithms are supported, just like in custom pools of the real GPU memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18938:See enum #VmaVirtualBlockCreateFlagBits to learn how to specify them (e.g. #VMA_VIRTUAL_BLOCK_CREATE_LINEAR_ALGORITHM_BIT).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18939:You can find their description in chapter \ref custom_memory_pools.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18940:Allocation strategies are also supported.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18941:See enum #VmaVirtualAllocationCreateFlagBits to learn how to specify them (e.g. #VMA_VIRTUAL_ALLOCATION_CREATE_STRATEGY_MIN_TIME_BIT).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18942:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18943:Following features are supported only by the allocator of the real GPU memory and not by virtual allocations:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18944:buffer-image granularity, `VMA_DEBUG_MARGIN`, `VMA_MIN_ALIGNMENT`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18945:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18946:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18947:\page debugging_memory_usage Debugging incorrect memory usage
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18948:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18949:If you suspect a bug with memory usage, like usage of uninitialized memory or
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18950:memory being overwritten out of bounds of an allocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18951:you can use debug features of this library to verify this.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18952:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18953:\section debugging_memory_usage_initialization Memory initialization
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18954:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18955:If you experience a bug with incorrect and nondeterministic data in your program and you suspect uninitialized memory to be used,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18956:you can enable automatic memory initialization to verify this.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18957:To do it, define macro `VMA_DEBUG_INITIALIZE_ALLOCATIONS` to 1.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18958:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18959:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18960:#define VMA_DEBUG_INITIALIZE_ALLOCATIONS 1
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18961:#include "vk_mem_alloc.h"
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18962:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18963:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18964:It makes memory of new allocations initialized to bit pattern `0xDCDCDCDC`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18965:Before an allocation is destroyed, its memory is filled with bit pattern `0xEFEFEFEF`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18966:Memory is automatically mapped and unmapped if necessary.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18967:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18968:If you find these values while debugging your program, good chances are that you incorrectly
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18969:read Vulkan memory that is allocated but not initialized, or already freed, respectively.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18970:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18971:Memory initialization works only with memory types that are `HOST_VISIBLE` and with allocations that can be mapped.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18972:It works also with dedicated allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18973:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18974:\section debugging_memory_usage_margins Margins
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18975:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18976:By default, allocations are laid out in memory blocks next to each other if possible
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18977:(considering required alignment, `bufferImageGranularity`, and `nonCoherentAtomSize`).
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18978:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18979:![Allocations without margin](../gfx/Margins_1.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18980:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18981:Define macro `VMA_DEBUG_MARGIN` to some non-zero value (e.g. 16) to enforce specified
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18982:number of bytes as a margin after every allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18983:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18984:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18985:#define VMA_DEBUG_MARGIN 16
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18986:#include "vk_mem_alloc.h"
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18987:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18988:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18989:![Allocations with margin](../gfx/Margins_2.png)
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18990:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18991:If your bug goes away after enabling margins, it means it may be caused by memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18992:being overwritten outside of allocation boundaries. It is not 100% certain though.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18993:Change in application behavior may also be caused by different order and distribution
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18994:of allocations across memory blocks after margins are applied.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18995:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18996:Margins work with all types of memory.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18997:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18998:Margin is applied only to allocations made out of memory blocks and not to dedicated
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:18999:allocations, which have their own memory block of specific size.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19000:It is thus not applied to allocations made using #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT flag
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19001:or those automatically decided to put into dedicated allocations, e.g. due to its
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19002:large size or recommended by VK_KHR_dedicated_allocation extension.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19003:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19004:Margins appear in [JSON dump](@ref statistics_json_dump) as part of free space.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19005:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19006:Note that enabling margins increases memory usage and fragmentation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19007:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19008:Margins do not apply to \ref virtual_allocator.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19009:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19010:\section debugging_memory_usage_corruption_detection Corruption detection
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19011:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19012:You can additionally define macro `VMA_DEBUG_DETECT_CORRUPTION` to 1 to enable validation
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19013:of contents of the margins.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19014:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19015:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19016:#define VMA_DEBUG_MARGIN 16
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19017:#define VMA_DEBUG_DETECT_CORRUPTION 1
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19018:#include "vk_mem_alloc.h"
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19019:\endcode
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19020:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19021:When this feature is enabled, number of bytes specified as `VMA_DEBUG_MARGIN`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19022:(it must be multiply of 4) after every allocation is filled with a magic number.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19023:This idea is also know as "canary".
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19024:Memory is automatically mapped and unmapped if necessary.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19025:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19026:This number is validated automatically when the allocation is destroyed.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19027:If it is not equal to the expected value, `VMA_ASSERT()` is executed.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19028:It clearly means that either CPU or GPU overwritten the memory outside of boundaries of the allocation,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19029:which indicates a serious bug.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19030:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19031:You can also explicitly request checking margins of all allocations in all memory blocks
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19032:that belong to specified memory types by using function vmaCheckCorruption(),
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19033:or in memory blocks that belong to specified custom pool, by using function
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19034:vmaCheckPoolCorruption().
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19035:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19036:Margin validation (corruption detection) works only for memory types that are
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19037:`HOST_VISIBLE` and `HOST_COHERENT`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19038:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19039:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19040:\section debugging_memory_usage_leak_detection Leak detection features
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19041:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19042:At allocation and allocator destruction time VMA checks for unfreed and unmapped blocks using
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19043:`VMA_ASSERT_LEAK()`. This macro defaults to an assertion, triggering a typically fatal error in Debug
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19044:builds, and doing nothing in Release builds. You can provide your own definition of `VMA_ASSERT_LEAK()`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19045:to change this behavior.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19046:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19047:At memory block destruction time VMA lists out all unfreed allocations using the `VMA_LEAK_LOG_FORMAT()`
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19048:macro, which defaults to `VMA_DEBUG_LOG_FORMAT`, which in turn defaults to a no-op.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19049:If you're having trouble with leaks - for example, the aforementioned assertion triggers, but you don't
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19050:quite know \em why -, overriding this macro to print out the the leaking blocks, combined with assigning
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19051:individual names to allocations using vmaSetAllocationName(), can greatly aid in fixing them.

src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19200:Documentation of the VK_KHR_external_memory_win32 extension states that:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19201:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19202:> If handleType is defined as an NT handle, vkGetMemoryWin32HandleKHR must be called no more than once for each valid unique combination of memory and handleType.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19203:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19204:This is ensured automatically inside VMA.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19205:If `VK_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_HANDLE_TYPE_OPAQUE_WIN32_BIT` is used as the handle type,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19206:or other NT handle types,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19207:the library fetches the handle on first use, remembers it internally, and closes it when the memory block or dedicated allocation is destroyed.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19208:Every time you call vmaGetMemoryWin32Handle2(), VMA calls `DuplicateHandle` and returns a new handle that you need to close.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19209:For further information, please check the documentation of this function.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19210:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19211:\subsection other_api_interop_exporting_custom_alignment Custom alignment
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19212:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19213:Buffers or images exported to a different API like OpenGL may require a different alignment,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19214:higher than the one used by the library automatically, queried from functions like `vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19215:To impose such alignment:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19216:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19217:You can create \ref custom_memory_pools for such allocations.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19218:Set VmaPoolCreateInfo::minAllocationAlignment member to the minimum alignment required for each allocation
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19219:to be made out of this pool.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19220:The alignment actually used will be the maximum of this member and the alignment returned for the specific buffer or image
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19221:from a function like `vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements`, which is called by VMA automatically.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19222:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19223:If you want to create a buffer/image/allocate memory with a specific minimum alignment out of default pools,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19224:you can use VmaAllocationCreateInfo::minAlignment.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19225:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19226:Note the problem of alignment affects only resources placed inside bigger `VkDeviceMemory` blocks and not dedicated
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19227:allocations, as these, by definition, always have alignment = 0 because the resource is bound to the beginning of its dedicated block.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19228:You can ensure that an allocation is created as dedicated by using #VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19229:Contrary to Direct3D 12, Vulkan doesn't have a concept of alignment of the entire memory block passed on its allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19230:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19231:\subsection other_api_interop_exporting_extended_allocation_information Extended allocation information
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19232:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19233:If you want to rely on VMA to allocate your buffers and images inside larger memory blocks,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19234:but you need to know the size of the entire block and whether the allocation was made
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19235:with its own dedicated memory, use function vmaGetAllocationInfo2() to retrieve
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19236:extended allocation information in structure #VmaAllocationInfo2, which provides extra members:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19237:`blockSize` and `dedicatedMemory`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19238:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19239:\section other_api_interop_importing_memory Importing memory
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19240:

src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19280:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19281:Vulkan gives great flexibility in memory allocation.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19282:This chapter shows the most common patterns.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19283:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19284:See also slides from talk:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19285:[Sawicki, Adam. Advanced Graphics Techniques Tutorial: Memory management in Vulkan and DX12. Game Developers Conference, 2018](https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1025458/Advanced-Graphics-Techniques-Tutorial-New)

src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19287:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19288:\section usage_patterns_gpu_only GPU-only resource
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19289:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19290:<b>When:</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19291:Any resources that you frequently write and read on GPU,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19292:e.g. images used as color attachments (aka "render targets"), depth-stencil attachments,
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19293:images/buffers used as storage image/buffer (aka "Unordered Access View (UAV)").
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19294:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19295:<b>What to do:</b>
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19296:Let the library select the optimal memory type, which will likely have `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT`.
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19297:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19298:\code
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19299:VkImageCreateInfo imgCreateInfo = { VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_CREATE_INFO };
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19300:imgCreateInfo.imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D;

src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19303:imgCreateInfo.extent.depth = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19304:imgCreateInfo.mipLevels = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19305:imgCreateInfo.arrayLayers = 1;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19306:imgCreateInfo.format = VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19307:imgCreateInfo.tiling = VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19308:imgCreateInfo.initialLayout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19309:imgCreateInfo.usage = VK_IMAGE_USAGE_SAMPLED_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19310:imgCreateInfo.samples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT;
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19311:
src/third_party/vk_mem_alloc.h:19312:VmaAllocationCreateInfo allocCreateInfo = {};
